# SQLite slice 2 — stream and cold restore — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A single venue continuously streams its database to an S3-compatible bucket the owner
supplies; a dead box can be rebuilt from that bucket with one recovery kit and trade again under a
fresh fiscal chain; staff can see how current the copy is.

**Architecture:** Litestream 0.5.17 runs as a child process of the server, supervised by a new
package, `@waitron/stream`, which also owns the bucket client, the signed pointer (`current.json`)
naming the live generation, generation housekeeping and the freshness figure. Everything the archive
carries except the database travels inside the stream, locked with the owner's recovery key, so a
rebuild through the existing restore path brings the box back whole. Per-machine rows stay in
`venue.db`, keyed by node id.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript on Node v26 (`node:sqlite`), Drizzle on SQLite, Hono, Lit (dashboard and
setup), Vitest (browser mode for the front-ends), `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, Litestream 0.5.17,
versitygw 1.8.0 (tests only).

**Spec:** [SQLite slice 2: stream and cold restore — design](../specs/2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).
Executors read the spec and this plan together; where they disagree, the spec's dated amendments and
the **Reconciliation** section below win over a task's text, and the disagreement is reported.

## Global Constraints

- Litestream is pinned at **0.5.17**; a bump re-runs Task 4's measurements and the prototype rig.
- The stream goes to **S3-compatible buckets only**; a bucket that fails the conditional-write probe
  is refused.
- Litestream settings: `snapshot.interval: 24h`, `snapshot.retention: 168h` (one full copy a day,
  7 days' history).
- Side-file limit **256 MiB**; `backup.stream_behind` at **15 minutes** of lag; the rebuild's
  "old box still looks alive" check at **10 minutes**.
- **Nothing external may block a sale, and the stream never makes `/health` fail.**
- **One recovery key per venue.** The recovery kit (bucket details, venue id, recovery key, pointer
  signer's public key) is as sensitive as the key, and every screen that shows it says so.
- **A rebuild asks the owner for one thing: the recovery kit.** No configuration is re-entered.
- **The venue id is the node's location id** (`config.till.locationId`).
- Pre-production: schema changes **regenerate** migrations with drizzle-kit; no data-migration code
  (CLAUDE.md §3). Verify each regeneration with `scripts/schema-constraints.test.ts` and
  `scripts/append-only-triggers.test.ts`.
- Every package holds **98/98/98/95** coverage; `@waitron/stream` joins `HIGH_BAR_PACKAGES` in
  `scripts/coverage-thresholds.test.ts` and the shard lists the day it is created. (2026-09-24: that
  list was retired by #549, so the `HIGH_BAR_PACKAGES` step does not apply.)
- **No package suite starts a container.** The loop test runs versitygw and Litestream as plain child
  processes, downloaded per CI run (the Actions cache is at its budget).
- Error codes name the domain concept, follow their siblings' prefix (`backup.stream_*`,
  `restore.stream_*`), and are never renamed once shipped; alerts carry English and Spanish wording.
- One pull request per task, from a worktree made with `python3 ~/workspace/tools/worktree.py new
  waitron <branch>`; every commit `git commit -s`; commit messages and PR text in plain English.
- Focused tests while implementing; `pnpm format:check` in every task's verify step; no
  whole-workspace local runs — CI runs the package suites.

## Review Focus

Five inputs no task's tests were written around, most likely first. Each line names the owning task,
where its test has been added.

1. **The box's clock is wrong by minutes** (a box without network time). Freshness must not report
   "current" when the bucket is behind, and generation names must stay unique. Owner: Task 7
   (`computeLag` with `skewMs` both ways: "does not read a bucket whose clock runs ahead…" beside
   "converts the bucket's clock…", plus a deletion proof — test only, the conversion exists) and
   Task 5 ("keeps two same-second openings apart whatever the clocks say…" in `generations.test.ts`
   — test only, the name and the create-only marker already do it).
2. **The owner supplies the wrong recovery kit** — another venue's, a truncated paste, a kit from
   before a key rotation. The rebuild refuses before anything on the box changes, naming what is
   wrong. Owner: Task 9b ("refuses another venue's kit…", "refuses a kit whose signing key is another
   venue's…", the existing "refuses the wrong recovery key", and the command line's "refuses a kit cut
   short by name…") and Task 9c (the wizard's words for each) — tests only; the refusals exist. A
   kit that is wholly another venue's (its bucket, key and signer all that venue's) restores that
   venue: a blank box has nothing to compare it with.
3. **Power is cut while Litestream is running** — on the next start the supervisor finds a stale
   Litestream state folder and possibly an orphaned child on a development machine; it starts cleanly
   and the lock is free. Owner: Task 6 ("starts cleanly after a power cut…", plus a deletion proof —
   test only, `#startChild` already deletes the folder) and Task 3a ("does not stay locked after the
   holder is killed", already in its plan). An orphaned Litestream child is stopped at the next start
   when its recorded PID's command line is this box's own (Task 6, "stops a leftover…" and "leaves
   alone a process…", Reconciliation N21), and `pnpm reap` sweeps parentless test copies.
4. **The bucket's key is revoked, or the bucket deleted, while the venue trades.** Sales continue at
   their normal speed, `backup.stream_bucket_unusable` is raised once, and the supervisor backs off
   rather than restarting Litestream in a tight loop. Owner: Task 6 ("restarts a Litestream that
   keeps exiting at once no faster than the backoff…" — test only), with the raised-once half in
   Task 7 ("names a key revoked while streaming once…" — test only; Task 7's bucket reads are what
   notice it) and the sale-speed half in Task 10's loop test ("sales keep their normal time with
   the S3 server stopped", against real Litestream); Task 7's "returns from start() at once while
   the bucket never answers, and hears every commit" pins only that starting does not wait.
5. **The disk fills during a rebuild's download.** The restore stops before anything on the box
   changes, removes its partial side file, and says the disk is full. Owner: Task 9b ("says the disk
   is full, removes the partial download and changes nothing", "says the disk filled when
   Litestream's error is…", the command line's "says the disk is full in words") and Task 9c (the
   wizard's words) — IMPLEMENTATION needed and planned: `restoreGeneration` reports `diskFull`, and
   the new code `restore.stream_disk_full`.

## Reconciliation

The tasks below were drafted in parallel against one contract and then reconciled. The decisions and
names that reconciliation settled are listed here, because they are the ones an implementer reading a
single task is most likely to get wrong.


### Owner decisions taken during planning (2026-09-23)

- O1. **A login survives a rebuild and a promotion.** Sessions and the other identity tables are venue
  data (`state`), not keyed by node. (Task 1a/1b already do this.)
- O2. **Up to 5,000 product images; shrink them on upload.** New Task 0, first in the order.
- O3. **Break-glass and `waitron-credentials` keep working beside a running server** (the lock's
  `exclusive: false` exemptions in Task 3a). Everything else — a second server above all — is refused.
  (2026-09-24: as built, three scripts also open without the lock — `record-one-sale.ts`,
  `settle-invoice-first.ts` and `cloud-backup-fixture.ts`'s capture step — and `deploy/waitron.sh`'s
  stamp read opens `venue.db` with its own read-only `node:sqlite` connection, not through the store,
  so it takes no lock either; see `docs/developers/conventions-data.md`, "One process per venue
  folder".)
- O4. **An archive restore ALSO gets the first-start routine** of Task 9a: a certificate re-issued
  for this machine's addresses and a membership document one term higher. Task 9a triggers on a marker
  written by BOTH restore sources (Task 9b's stream path and the existing archive path), not the stream
  path only; its tests cover both.
- O5. **One recovery key per venue.** Turning archives on when streaming already set a key REUSES it;
  it never mints a second. A new kit is offered only on an explicit rotation. (Tasks 2a, 8a, 8b.)
- O6. **A box never replaces a pointer that names a higher term than its own** — it stops streaming and
  raises `backup.stream_refused`. (Task 6 already has it; Task 5's `writePointer` callers must not
  bypass it.)
- O7. Defaults the owner was told and did not change: `tenant_credentials` stays `local` with no node
  id (slice 3 replaces the per-machine key); the side-file limit is 256 MiB.
- O8. **The image upload limit rises from 5 MiB to 20 MiB.** Stored images are the shrunk copies
  (about 170 KB each), so the limit bounds the upload, not what is stored; the decode is bounded by
  `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000`, which stays (decoding a 100-megapixel image raised memory by
  about 29 MiB, measured by Task 0's drafter).
  Task 0 changes `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, the route's fallback and every test and document that states
  the limit. The configuration-transfer check (`MAX_BYTES`, 5 MiB) stays, because it checks stored
  bytes, not uploads.
- O9. **Use sharp.** libvips is LGPL-3.0-or-later, loaded as its own shared library
  (`libvips-cpp.so.8.18.6`, from `@img/sharp-libvips-<platform>`; confirmed from the installed
  binary's NEEDED/RPATH entries). Task 0 ships the LGPL-3.0 text (with the GPL-3.0 it incorporates),
  the libvips package's notices and a written source offer in the box image under
  `/app/third-party/` (new: nothing in the repository or the image kept third-party notices), and
  adds one open question for the legal advisor to `docs/compliance/action-plan.md`.

### Names and ownership

- N1. **Task order:** 0, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 3a, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8a, 8b, 9a, 9b, 9c, 10. Task 3b LANDED
  as #513 before this plan was committed (see its section); Task 3a's lock is what makes it safe.
- N2. **Task 2's names are the T2-3 draft's:** `apps/server/src/sealed-state.ts`, table
  `node_sealed_state`, `collectSealedEntries`, `sealNodeState`, `unsealNodeState` (synchronous),
  `writeSealedStateRow`, `readSealedStateRow`, `createSealedStateRefresher(...).refresh()`.
  `loadRecoveryKey` and `writeRecoveryKey` are defined ONCE, in Task 2a; Task 8a consumes them and
  defines neither. Replace every `unsealRecoveryState`, `readRecoveryStateRow`, `collectRecoveryEntries`,
  `recovery-state.ts` (which is an existing, unrelated file — the boot failure counter) in later tasks.
- N3. **Error codes for `@waitron/stream` and the stream feature are `backup.stream_*`** (Task 5's
  choice: every backup code is `backup.*`). `stream.precondition_failed` → `backup.stream_precondition_failed`;
  `stream.kit_invalid` → `backup.stream_kit_invalid`; `stream.restore_failed` → `backup.stream_restore_failed`.
  Restore-path codes stay `restore.stream_*` (siblings `restore.archive_incomplete` etc. exist in
  `apps/server/src/errors.ts`). Settings codes `backup.stream_test_failed`, `backup.stream_not_configured`,
  `backup.stream_signer_missing` stand.
- N4. **The lock's error is `provisioning.database_in_use` with `{ database }`** (Task 3a). Replace
  `store.venue_in_use` everywhere (Task 10 has two).
- N5. **The Litestream binary:** setup script `scripts/setup-litestream.ts` (TypeScript — Task 6's
  reason: the root coverage gate measures every `scripts/**/*.mjs`; corrected 2026-09-24: it is now
  `scripts/setup-litestream.mjs`, measured by that gate, see contract change 5); installs to `<repo>/.bin/litestream`
  (gitignored `/.bin/`); the server finds it through `WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN`. Task 6 exports, from
  `@waitron/stream`, `LITESTREAM_VERSION` and `resolveLitestreamBin(env): string`, which returns the
  default path — never throws — when the variable is unset. Task 10 uses `.ts`, not `.mjs`;
  corrected 2026-09-24: Task 10 now names `scripts/setup-litestream.mjs`, see contract change 5.
- N6. **One replica-location function, defined in Task 6**, used by Task 6's config writer and Task
  9b's restore. Name it `replicaUrl(bucket, venueId, generation): string`, returning the `s3://…` URL
  Litestream takes, built on Task 5's `bucketKey`/`venuePrefix` (keys are relative to the owner's
  prefix). Task 6's `replicaPath` is folded into it.
- N7. **`restoreGeneration({ litestreamBin, bucket, venueId, generation, outPath })`** lives in
  `@waitron/stream` and is defined in Task 9b (its draft already writes it); Task 10 consumes it.
- N8. **`StreamHost` moves into Task 6.** Task 6 wires boot, so it owns the host that builds and
  rebuilds a `StreamSupervisor` when the bucket settings change. Task 7's `/health` reads
  `streamHost.status()`; Task 8a's routes call the host to apply or remove settings.
- N9. **The venue id is the node's location id** (`config.till.locationId`; boot already treats it as
  the single operational venue, `assertSingleOperationalVenue` in `apps/server/src/boot.ts`). The
  `backup.stream` credentials purpose carries a `venueId` field (Task 6's definition), which Task 8a
  WRITES from `config.till.locationId` when settings are saved; the recovery kit carries it; a rebuild
  uses the kit's.
- N10. **The `backup.stream` purpose is defined once, in Task 6** (fields `endpoint`, `region`,
  `bucket`, `prefix`, `accessKeyId`, `secretAccessKey`, `venueId`; an absent endpoint or prefix is
  stored as `-`, the SumUp purpose's convention). Task 8a does not redefine it.
- N11. **The restore command:** `waitron-restore --from-bucket <kit-file>`, plus
  `--confirm-old-box-gone`, which is REQUIRED only when the liveness check trips (a change file in the
  live generation within the last 10 minutes). `runRestore` returns 0 on success. Task 9b and Task 10
  must agree.
- N12. **Pointer signing:** `sign(message: string)` in `SupervisorDeps`; Task 5 exports
  `pointerMessage(body)`, `signPointer(body, privateKey)`, `verifyPointer(pointer, publicKeySpki)`.
- N13. **`probeBucket(store, nonce?)`** returns `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false; reason: <fixed list>;
  detail: string }` and throws only when the bucket gave no answer. Task 8a translates each reason.
- N14. **`foldBack()` / `checkpointTruncate()` return `{ reclaimed: boolean }` and run on the WRITER
  connection in a write-queue slot with no transaction** (Task 6's measurement: from a separate
  connection it waits out the busy timeout, freezing the synchronous process).
- N15. **Freshness input** is Task 7's: `computeLag({ pending, newestUploadAt, skewMs, now })` →
  `{ lagMs, coveredUpTo }`, with `CommitLog` bounding pending commits.
- N16. **`writeValidated`'s order (Tasks 3a and 9a):** take the venue lock → write the first-start
  marker → `placeValidated` → release. On failure the marker is removed while the lock is still
  held. A restore refused by the lock writes no marker.
- N17. **`restoreGeneration` (Task 9b) reuses Task 6's pieces:** its configuration comes from
  `litestreamConfig` (which refuses a `$`), and its child from `spawnLitestream` (PATH, HOME and the
  two bucket-key variables only — never the whole process environment).
- N18. **A bucket restore is bounded by activity, not a fixed time:** abandoned when its output has
  not grown for 2 minutes (`RESTORE_STALL_MS`), with a 6-hour absolute ceiling as a backstop only
  (`RESTORE_CEILING_MS`).
- N19. **The "old box still alive" check runs on the bucket's clock.** It measures the difference
  from a probe object's `LastModified` (as Task 7 does from its marker) and applies it; when the
  difference cannot be measured it refuses with `restore.stream_source_unchecked { reason: "clock" }`
  until the operator confirms the old box is gone.
- N20. **The supervisor never logs Litestream's output** — the recovery page shows the log tail
  unauthenticated (`apps/server/src/recovery-surface.ts`). It logs the exit code and a fixed
  category (`exitCategory`: `disk_full`, `bucket_refused`, `bucket_unreachable`, `signal`, `other`).
- N21. **A leftover Litestream is stopped by PID and command line.** The supervisor records its
  child's PID in `<configDir>/litestream.pid` and, at start, stops a process with that PID only when
  its command line is `replicate -config <this configuration>`. `pnpm reap` also kills parentless
  `.bin/litestream` and `.bin/versitygw` processes, matched by the path's shape, never a bare name.
- N22. **Boot order (Tasks 2b and 6):** `await backupSupervisor.reload();`, then the sealed-state
  refresh, then `streamHost.start()` — the refresh comes BEFORE the stream starts, both after the
  reload.
- N23. **(Lead decision.) The first start after ANY restore signs its membership document at term =
  max(restored term, the bucket pointer's term when bucket settings exist and the pointer is
  readable) + 1** (Task 9a, `minTerm`, `readBucketPointerTerm`). An archive restore whose restored
  database holds bucket settings runs N19's old-box check before staging, and before the command
  line places anything (Task 9b's `refuseIfArchiveSourceLive`; a bucket that gives no answer refuses
  with `restore.stream_source_unchecked { reason: "bucket" }`).
- N24. **(Lead decision.) A failed first start does not keep the box shut.** If `completeRebuild`
  fails, the box opens for sales, does NOT start streaming, raises the ongoing alert
  `restore.first_start_failed` (English and Spanish wording), and retries at the next start (the
  marker stays) — Task 9a's `runFirstStart`.
- N25. **Generation pruning is wired:** Task 6's supervisor calls Task 5's `pruneGenerations` from
  its streaming tick, at most once a day, with the live generation's name and 168 hours; the call
  is not awaited, so a bucket that never answers cannot hold the tick.
- N26. **The owner confirms whose copy it is before staging.** `prepareStreamRestore` returns the
  restored copy's legal name, tax id and location name (`tenants`, `locations`); the command line
  needs `--confirm-venue <tax id>` and the wizard a "This is my business" confirmation, else
  `restore.stream_venue_unconfirmed` carrying the three.
- N27. **Rebased onto `origin/main` at `c9d0c5cbe`.** PR #511 already made `tablesCreatedBy` follow
  `ALTER TABLE … RENAME TO` (Task 1a no longer adds it), and the core set already holds migrations
  `0000`–`0004`, one of which rebuilds `products`; migration numbers are drizzle-kit's to choose.
- N28. **Main moved while this plan was written; #513 landed Task 3b.** #513 also rewrote the
  backlog entry for the restart reset, added dated pointers to the design documents that said "not
  built", and corrected spec §6's account of error 3000 (a copy AEAT reports as accepted is marked
  accepted with no fingerprint comparison; only an annulled copy, or one whose state AEAT does not
  give, goes to `handleDuplicate`). Task 10's documentation sweep checks what #513 already wrote and
  does not add a second pointer or rewrite its entry. Rebase each task onto current `main` before
  starting it; line citations in this plan were taken against `a1934f1c6` or earlier.

### Litestream's own footprint (Task 10's measurement, confirmed from source by Task 6)

- L1. Litestream 0.5.17 creates `_litestream_seq` and `_litestream_lock` tables inside `venue.db`
  and a `.venue.db-litestream/` directory beside it. A restored copy carries the two tables.
- L2. Every guard or check that enumerates tables of a LIVE or restored database must leave
  `_litestream_*` out explicitly (name each one the plan touches: Task 9b's integrity/compatibility
  path, Task 10's equality check; the implementer greps for others that read `sqlite_master`).
- L3. `apps/server/src/db-wipe.ts` and `restore.ts`'s `restoreDatabase` remove `.venue.db-litestream/`
  together with `venue.db`, `-wal` and `-shm` (Task 9b owns both edits, with a test that a stale
  directory beside a replaced database is gone afterwards). Task 6 deletes it before opening a new
  generation.
- L4. The prototype rig stays as a record, but MinIO is no longer a live reference: its repository is
  archived and its binaries are no longer published. The loop test's server is **versitygw 1.8.0**
  (Task 10), with SeaweedFS as the recorded fallback.

Create `packages/media/src/testing/sample-image.ts`:

```ts
import sharp from "sharp";

/**
 * A small solid-colour picture that sharp can decode, for tests that upload.
 *
 * Within ONE format, two different widths always store as two different photos. This was measured
 * for widths 8 to 307 at height 6 in each format. A JPEG and a PNG of the same width store as the
 * SAME photo, because a solid colour decodes identically from both, so a suite needing distinct
 * photos varies the width, not the format.
 */
export async function sampleImage(options: {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  format: "jpeg" | "png" | "webp";
}): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const image = sharp({
    create: {
      width: options.width,
      height: options.height,
      channels: 3,
      background: { r: 200, g: 120, b: 40 },
    },
  });
  return new Uint8Array(await image.toFormat(options.format).toBuffer());
}
```

```ts
    .jpeg({ quality: 50 })

      .jpeg()
```

Create `packages/media/src/prepare.ts`:

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { validateImageBytes } from "@waitron/catalogue";
import { AppError } from "@waitron/shared";
import "./errors.js";

/**
 * The longer side, in pixels, of every photo the library stores: enough for a photo 800 CSS pixels
 * wide on a screen with two device pixels per CSS pixel. With `STORED_WEBP_QUALITY` a real photo
 * averages about 170 KiB, so 5,000 photos take about 0.9 GB of the venue database.
 */
export const STORED_LONG_EDGE = 1600;
/** sharp's WebP quality, on its 1–100 scale. */
export const STORED_WEBP_QUALITY = 80;
/** The most pixels an upload may declare. Checked from the header, before anything is decoded. */
export const MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000;

/** Exported and `declare`d only for the brand below, the pattern `packages/shared/src/ids.ts` explains. */
export declare const preparedImageBrand: unique symbol;

/**
 * A photo ready to store. It is shrunk to at most `STORED_LONG_EDGE` on its longer side, never
 * enlarged, turned upright, stripped of every metadata block (EXIF with any GPS position, XMP and
 * ICC), and re-encoded as WebP. `filename` is the sha256 of THESE bytes plus their sniffed
 * extension, so `/media/<filename>`, served `immutable`, names exactly what it serves. Only
 * `prepareImage` makes one.
 */
export interface PreparedImage {
  readonly bytes: Uint8Array;
  readonly filename: string;
  readonly [preparedImageBrand]: true;
}

type Sharp = typeof import("sharp").default;
let loading: Promise<Sharp> | undefined;

/**
 * sharp is loaded on first use, not at import. Bundles that never prepare a photo, such as
 * `waitron-provision`, reach this module and run with no sharp installed beside them. The server
 * bundle leaves sharp out (`--external:sharp`) and the box image puts it in `/app/node_modules`.
 * One libvips thread (sharp's own default on glibc Linux, the box's platform) and no operation cache,
 * so an upload takes neither every core nor memory it keeps afterwards from the process serving sales.
 */
function loadSharp(): Promise<Sharp> {
  loading ??= import("sharp").then(({ default: sharp }) => {
    sharp.concurrency(1);
    sharp.cache(false);
    return sharp;
  });
  return loading;
}

/**
 * Turns an upload into the bytes the library stores. Call it OUTSIDE any transaction. The decode
 * takes long enough that holding the venue's one write lock (`withTransaction`) for it would make
 * every other write wait.
 */
export async function prepareImage(
  bytes: Uint8Array,
  options: { maxUploadBytes: number },
): Promise<PreparedImage> {
  if (bytes.length > options.maxUploadBytes)
    throw new AppError("image.too_large", { maxBytes: options.maxUploadBytes });
  validateImageBytes(bytes);
  const sharp = await loadSharp();
  let declared: { width: number; height: number };
  try {
    declared = await sharp(bytes).metadata();
  } catch {
    throw new AppError("image.invalid_file", {});
  }
  if (declared.width * declared.height > MAX_INPUT_PIXELS)
    throw new AppError("image.too_many_pixels", { maxPixels: MAX_INPUT_PIXELS });
  let output: Buffer;
  try {
    output = await sharp(bytes, {
      failOn: "warning",
      limitInputPixels: MAX_INPUT_PIXELS,
      autoOrient: true,
    })
      .resize(STORED_LONG_EDGE, STORED_LONG_EDGE, { fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true })
      .webp({ quality: STORED_WEBP_QUALITY })
      .toBuffer();
  } catch {
    throw new AppError("image.invalid_file", {});
  }
  const stored = new Uint8Array(output);
  return {
    bytes: stored,
    filename: `${createHash("sha256").update(stored).digest("hex")}.${validateImageBytes(stored)}`,
  } as PreparedImage;
}
```

Replace lines 203-225 (`uploadImage`) with:

```ts
/**
 * Adds a photo to the library, or returns the existing entry when one already stores these exact
 * bytes. Takes a `PreparedImage`, so every stored photo has been through `prepareImage`: shrunk,
 * upright, stripped of metadata and re-encoded.
 */
export async function uploadImage(
  tx: Transaction,
  input: ImageMetadataInput & { image: PreparedImage },
  options: UploadImageOptions = {},
): Promise<{ created: boolean; image: ImageRecord }> {
  const { filename, bytes } = input.image;
  const values = await metadata(tx, input, options.fallbackLanguage ?? FALLBACK_LOCALE);
  // The content-language lock also serializes duplicate uploads.
  const [existing] = await tx
    .select({ id: mediaImages.id })
    .from(mediaImages)
    .where(eq(mediaImages.filename, filename));
  if (existing) return { created: false, image: await readImage(tx, existing.id) };
  const [row] = await tx
    .insert(mediaImages)
    .values({ filename, ...values })
    .returning({ id: mediaImages.id });
  await tx.insert(mediaImageData).values({ imageId: row!.id, bytes });
  return { created: true, image: await readImage(tx, row!.id) };
}
```

In `scripts/deploy-image-env.test.ts`, change line 1 to
`import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";` and append:

```ts
/**
 * sharp is a native addon with a shared library beside it, and esbuild does not refuse to bundle
 * it. Without `--external:sharp` the build exits 0 and the first upload fails with `Dynamic require
 * of "…" is not supported`. Measured on esbuild 0.28.2.
 *
 * Reads TEXT. It finds the esbuild bundles that can reach `@waitron/media` by following `dependencies`
 * through workspace package.json files, so a reach through a devDependency or a relative import
 * across packages is invisible to it. It counts flags, so it cannot tell which command a flag
 * belongs to.
 */
describe("sharp stays outside every bundle and ships beside the server's", () => {
  type Manifest = {
    name: string;
    dependencies?: Record<string, string>;
    scripts?: Record<string, string>;
  };
  const manifests = new Map<string, Manifest>();
  for (const root of ["apps", "packages"]) {
    for (const dir of readdirSync(`${ROOT}${root}`)) {
      const path = `${root}/${dir}/package.json`;
      if (!existsSync(`${ROOT}${path}`)) continue;
      const manifest = JSON.parse(read(path)) as Manifest;
      manifests.set(manifest.name, manifest);
    }
  }
  const reachesMedia = (name: string, seen = new Set<string>()): boolean => {
    if (name === "@waitron/media") return true;
    if (seen.has(name)) return false;
    seen.add(name);
    return Object.keys(manifests.get(name)?.dependencies ?? {}).some(
      (dependency) => manifests.has(dependency) && reachesMedia(dependency, seen),
    );
  };
  const bundlers = [...manifests.values()].filter(
    (manifest) => (manifest.scripts?.build ?? "").includes("esbuild ") && reachesMedia(manifest.name),
  );

  it("finds the bundles it is meant to check", () => {
    expect(bundlers.map((manifest) => manifest.name)).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining(["@waitron/server", "@waitron/provisioning"]),
    );
  });

  it.each(bundlers.map((manifest) => [manifest.name, manifest.scripts!.build!]))(
    "%s names --external:sharp on every esbuild command",
    (_name, build) => {
      const commands = build.split("esbuild ").length - 1;
      expect(commands).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      expect(build.split("--external:sharp").length - 1).toBe(commands);
    },
  );

  it("copies sharp beside the bundle in the image, and both CI jobs check it", () => {
    expect(DOCKERFILE).toContain("/sharp-runtime/node_modules/ /app/node_modules/");
    expect(CI).toContain(`grep -q 'import("sharp")' apps/server/dist/server.js`);
    expect(IMAGE_SMOKE).toContain("await import('sharp')");
  });
});
```

`docs/content-and-images.md`: add after the first paragraph of "Add a photograph once":

```markdown
Waitron keeps a smaller copy of each photograph rather than the file you chose. A phone photo is
often several megabytes, and a library of thousands of them would make every backup and every
restore slow, so Waitron resizes each upload to at most 1600 pixels on its longer side, keeps its
shape, and saves it in the WebP format, which every current browser shows. That is still larger
than anywhere Waitron draws it. A photo that is already smaller is never enlarged. Waitron also
removes the hidden details cameras add, such as where and when the photo was taken, because
anyone who has a photo's address can open it. Files up to 20 MB are accepted. If a photo is
refused as too large, has too many pixels or cannot be read, export a smaller copy from your
photo app and upload that instead.
```

(The last sentence of the second paragraph under "Find and reuse an image", "Uploading the same file
again finds the existing image…", stays true and is unchanged.)

`docs/backlog.md`: add after the image-library "What that leaves open" list:

```markdown
**Photos are shrunk on upload (slice 2, Task 0, 2026-09-23).** Every upload is resized to at most
1600 pixels on its longer side, turned upright, stripped of its metadata (GPS position included) and
stored as WebP at quality 80 by `prepareImage` (`packages/media/src/prepare.ts`), outside the write
transaction. Measured on ten real food photos, a stored photo averages 171 KiB, so 5,000 take about
0.87 GB instead of about 18 GB. sharp does the work; the server bundle leaves it out and the box
image carries it in `/app/node_modules`.

What it leaves open:

- **The upload limit is 20 MB (owner decision 2026-09-23, up from 5 MB).** It limits what may be
  uploaded, not what is stored. The decode is bounded by `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS`, which refuses anything
  above 100 megapixels: a 100-megapixel picture raised memory by about 29 MiB when decoded
  (measured). What
  current phones produce has not been measured.
- **The library grid loads the full 1600-pixel copy for each tile.** A page of 40 photos is about
  7 MB on first load and is cached afterwards. A small thumbnail copy would help over slow Wi-Fi.
  Next action: decide whether the grid needs one.
- **Dev venues seeded before this keep full-size tiles** until `wa-wt reset demo <name>`.
- **libvips is LGPL-3.0-or-later** and now ships in the box image, with its licence texts, its
  notices and a written source offer in `/app/third-party/` (`deploy/third-party/`). The legal
  advisor is asked to confirm it (`docs/compliance/action-plan.md`, 2026-09-23).
```

```bash
git commit -s -m "Shrink photos on upload so the venue database stays small

Every uploaded photo is now resized to at most 1600 pixels on its longer
side, turned upright, stripped of its hidden details (including any GPS
position, which the public /media address used to serve to anyone) and
stored as WebP. prepareImage in packages/media/src/prepare.ts does this
with sharp, outside the write transaction, so an upload never holds the
venue's one write lock while it decodes. uploadImage now takes only a
prepared photo.

Measured on ten real 2.6-5.0 MB food photos: 170.7 KiB stored on average,
so 5,000 photos take about 0.87 GB instead of about 18 GB. Each photo took
131 ms on average on an Apple M5 Pro; the box's processor is unmeasured.
jSquash was about four times slower and blocked the event loop for the
whole shrink (1289 ms against sharp's 6 ms).

sharp cannot be bundled. Every esbuild command that reaches the media
package now passes --external:sharp, the box image copies sharp into
/app/node_modules, and three checks guard it: scripts/deploy-image-env.test.ts,
a grep of the built bundle in CI, and a sharp step in the image smoke job.

The upload limit rises from 5 MB to 20 MB: what is stored is the shrunk
copy, so the limit bounds the upload, not what is stored; the pixel limit
bounds the decode. libvips, which sharp loads as its own LGPL library, ships with its
licence texts, its notices and a written source offer in /app/third-party.
Photos already stored keep their bytes; dev venues get shrunk tiles on the
next wa-wt reset demo."
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the schema (first half, then generate)**

drizzle-kit rebuilds a table when its primary key, a check or a not-null flag changes, and the copy
step selects EVERY column of the new table from the old one. Read from drizzle-kit 0.31.10's
`bin.cjs`: `SQLiteRecreateTableConvertor.convert` builds `INSERT INTO __new_<t>(<new columns>) SELECT
<new columns> FROM <t>`, and `sqliteCombineStatements` replaces a table's add-column statement with
the rebuild. Measured 2026-09-23 on Node v26.7.0 / SQLite 3.53.4, in a scratch in-memory database:
that SELECT fails with `no such column: "token_hash"` even when the old table is EMPTY. So a new
NOT NULL column that also comes with a rebuild would fail on every database, a fresh one included.
The migration is therefore generated in two steps: first the new columns go in nullable, then a
second generate tightens them. A dev venue whose rows cannot satisfy the tightened column then fails
with the engine's NOT NULL refusal (1299), which `apps/server/src/dev-migration-hint.ts` recognises
and answers with the `wa-wt reset` hint. By contrast, a plain `ALTER TABLE … ADD … NOT NULL` on a
table that has rows fails with errcode 1, `Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL`
(same measurement), which the hint does not recognise.

Create `packages/db/src/schema/node-roles.ts`:

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { check } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
import { id, label, now, table, ts } from "./columns.js";

/**
 * This node's role in the venue, one row per node, keyed by the node's own id
 * (`WAITRON_TILL_NODE_ID`). Every read and write names that id, so a node holding another node's copy
 * of `venue.db` reads its own row or none; no row reads as a sole primary (`../deployment.ts`). The
 * environment is not here: it belongs to the database and stays on `deployment`.
 */
// The bracketed thunks below are resolved by `drizzle-kit generate` in its own CLI process,
// never by `vitest run`, so v8 reports them as never-invoked functions. Same treatment, and
// the same reason, as ./sales.ts.
export const nodeRoles = table(
  "node_roles",
  {
    // No foreign key to `nodes`: a `local` table holds none into a venue table
    // (`scripts/two-file-foreign-keys.test.ts`), and adopt writes a standby's role before its `nodes`
    // row exists — boot's adoption worker writes that later (`apps/server/src/adopt.ts`).
    nodeId: id("node_id").primaryKey(),
    // `primary` writes and originates; on a `mirror` boot mounts the read-only gate
    // (`apps/server/src/read-only-gate.ts`). Read at runtime so a promotion needs no restart.
    mode: label("mode").$type<"primary" | "mirror">().notNull().default("primary"),
    // Orthogonal to `mode`: `primary` holds the venue's singleton duties (AEAT submitter and
    // reconciler), `secondary` sells only.
    singletonRole: label("singleton_role").$type<"primary" | "secondary">().notNull().default("primary"),
    // A scrypt verifier of the offline break-glass secret, set at adopt. Never the secret itself.
    breakGlassVerifier: label("break_glass_verifier"),
    updatedAt: ts("updated_at").notNull().$defaultFn(now),
  },
  /* v8 ignore start */
  (t) => [
    check("node_roles_mode_ck", sql`${t.mode} in ('primary', 'mirror')`),
    check("node_roles_singleton_role_ck", sql`${t.singletonRole} in ('primary', 'secondary')`),
    check(
      "node_roles_role_valid_ck",
      sql`not (${t.mode} = 'mirror' and ${t.singletonRole} = 'primary')`,
    ),
  ],
  /* v8 ignore stop */
);
```

```ts
 * A cloud mirror's link to the box it was adopted from (sync cloud-mirror C2b), one row per node,

  originNodeId: id("origin_node_id").notNull(),
```

`packages/db/src/deployment.ts`. Keep `DeploymentEnvironment`, `deploymentTableExists`,
`readDeploymentEnvironment` and `stampDeployment` exactly as they are. Imports become:

```ts
import { eq, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { AppError } from "@waitron/shared";
import type { Database, Transaction } from "./client.js";
import { now } from "./schema/columns.js";
import { deployment } from "./schema/deployment.js";
import { nodeRoles } from "./schema/node-roles.js";
```

Replace everything from `export type DeploymentMode` to the end of the file with:

```ts
/** Which role a node plays — a `primary` writes and originates; a `mirror` holds no singleton duties
 * and boots behind a read-only gate. Narrowed so an unrepresentable value is a `tsc` error, not a
 * runtime CHECK violation. */
export type DeploymentMode = "primary" | "mirror";

/** Whether a node holds the venue's singleton duties (the AEAT submitter and payment reconciler) —
 * `primary` — or sells only. */
export type SingletonRole = "primary" | "secondary";

/** Whether `node_roles` exists behind this handle — read off the catalogue for the reason given on
 * {@link deploymentTableExists}. What lets the readers below answer before migrations have run. */
async function nodeRolesTableExists(db: Database): Promise<boolean> {
  const present = await db.execute<{ name: string }>(
    sql`select name from sqlite_master where type = 'table' and name = ${"node_roles"}`,
  );
  return present.rows.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Both of one node's axes, `mode` and `singleton_role`, from ONE read of that node's row, so the pair
 * is never torn — never the `(mirror, primary)` pair `node_roles_role_valid_ck` forbids. A node with no
 * row, or a database whose migrations have not run, reads as a sole primary: a box between its first
 * migration and its first role write must still sell.
 */
export async function readDeploymentAxes(
  db: Database,
  nodeId: string,
): Promise<{ mode: DeploymentMode; singletonRole: SingletonRole }> {
  if (!(await nodeRolesTableExists(db))) return { mode: "primary", singletonRole: "primary" };
  const [row] = await db
    .select({ mode: nodeRoles.mode, singletonRole: nodeRoles.singletonRole })
    .from(nodeRoles)
    .where(eq(nodeRoles.nodeId, nodeId));
  return { mode: row?.mode ?? "primary", singletonRole: row?.singletonRole ?? "primary" };
}

/** One node's mode; see {@link readDeploymentAxes}. */
export async function readDeploymentMode(db: Database, nodeId: string): Promise<DeploymentMode> {
  return (await readDeploymentAxes(db, nodeId)).mode;
}

/** One node's singleton role; see {@link readDeploymentAxes}. */
export async function readSingletonRole(db: Database, nodeId: string): Promise<SingletonRole> {
  return (await readDeploymentAxes(db, nodeId)).singletonRole;
}

/**
 * Refuses a role write on a database that has not been stamped with its environment. These are
 * promotion primitives: a mis-sequenced adopt or promote that "succeeded" before the stamp would leave
 * a node's role recorded on a database nothing has claimed for an environment.
 */
async function requireStamp(tx: Transaction): Promise<void> {
  const [row] = await tx.select({ id: deployment.id }).from(deployment).where(eq(deployment.id, 1));
  if (row === undefined) throw new AppError("deployment.not_stamped", {});
}

/** Sets one node's mode, on its own write transaction. See {@link setDeploymentModeTx}. */
export async function setDeploymentMode(
  db: Database,
  nodeId: string,
  mode: DeploymentMode,
): Promise<void> {
  await db.withWriteLock(async () => setDeploymentModeTx(db, nodeId, mode));
}

/**
 * Sets one node's mode on a caller's transaction, creating the node's row if it has none. `mirror`
 * co-sets `singleton_role = 'secondary'` in the same write, so the pair `node_roles_role_valid_ck`
 * forbids is never written even transiently; `primary` leaves `singleton_role` as it is — which of
 * the two a primary holds is the promote action's call. Nothing in the database refuses another
 * caller this write; `scripts/write-path-tables.test.ts` keeps it in this file.
 */
export async function setDeploymentModeTx(
  tx: Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
  mode: DeploymentMode,
): Promise<void> {
  await requireStamp(tx);
  await tx
    .insert(nodeRoles)
    .values({ nodeId, mode, singletonRole: mode === "mirror" ? "secondary" : "primary" })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({
      target: nodeRoles.nodeId,
      set:
        mode === "mirror"
          ? { mode, singletonRole: "secondary", updatedAt: now() }
          : { mode, updatedAt: now() },
    });
}

/** Sets one node's singleton role, on its own write transaction. See {@link setSingletonRoleTx}. */
export async function setSingletonRole(
  db: Database,
  nodeId: string,
  role: SingletonRole,
): Promise<void> {
  await db.withWriteLock(async () => setSingletonRoleTx(db, nodeId, role));
}

/** Sets one node's singleton role on a caller's transaction, creating the node's row (mode
 * `primary`) if it has none. `'primary'` on a node whose mode is `mirror` is refused by
 * `node_roles_role_valid_ck`: a promotion flips the mode first. */
export async function setSingletonRoleTx(
  tx: Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
  role: SingletonRole,
): Promise<void> {
  await requireStamp(tx);
  await tx
    .insert(nodeRoles)
    .values({ nodeId, singletonRole: role })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({
      target: nodeRoles.nodeId,
      set: { singletonRole: role, updatedAt: now() },
    });
}

/** One node's stored break-glass verifier, or `null` when it has none. Never the secret. */
export async function readBreakGlassVerifier(
  db: Database | Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const [row] = await db
    .select({ v: nodeRoles.breakGlassVerifier })
    .from(nodeRoles)
    .where(eq(nodeRoles.nodeId, nodeId));
  return row?.v ?? null;
}

/** Writes one node's break-glass verifier on a caller's transaction, creating the node's row if it
 * has none. The spec (§9.3) reserves this for adopt; nothing in the database refuses another writer. */
export async function setBreakGlassVerifierTx(
  tx: Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
  verifier: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await requireStamp(tx);
  await tx
    .insert(nodeRoles)
    .values({ nodeId, breakGlassVerifier: verifier })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({
      target: nodeRoles.nodeId,
      set: { breakGlassVerifier: verifier, updatedAt: now() },
    });
}
```

```ts
}
```

```bash
the scheduled-run record - are reclassified as venue state. The local
class now means a row that belongs to one node, rather than a table that
lives in node.db, and the guards and docs say so.
```

### Task 1b: Session cookies stored only as hashes

**Branch:** `feat/sqlite-slice2-hashed-sessions` (after 1a has merged)

**What each identity `local` table becomes:**

| Table | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions` | `state`, gains `token_hash` | a person's shift login at a till. The cookie is a bearer credential, so only its hash is stored and a copy of the database signs nobody in. Not keyed by node: see Open question 1 |
| `management_sessions` | `state`, gains `token_hash` | the same, for the dashboard |
| `webauthn_challenges` | `state`, unchanged | short-lived, and a challenge signs nobody in without the authenticator (spec §2) |
| `totp_enrollments` | `state`, unchanged | short-lived; its secret is stored encrypted (`encrypted_secret`) |
| `google_oidc_states` | `state`, unchanged | short-lived; its state is already stored as a hash (`state_hash`, spec §2) |

None of the three ceremony tables belongs to a machine: each belongs to a browser in the middle of a
sign-in. With them unkeyed, a ceremony started before a rebuild can be finished on the rebuilt box.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the token helpers and the first schema half**

Create `packages/identity/src/session-token.ts`:

```ts
import { createHash, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

/**
 * A new bearer token for a session cookie. A random v4 UUID — the same generator `newId` uses for
 * every row id (`packages/db/src/schema/columns.ts`), so a cookie carries what it carried when it was
 * the row id, and keeps the shape the `isUuid` screens check (`apps/server/src/till-session.ts`,
 * `packages/server-kit/src/management-cookie.ts`).
 */
export function mintSessionToken(): string {
  return randomUUID();
}

/**
 * What a session row stores in place of its token: lowercase hex SHA-256. A copy of the database —
 * a bucket, an archive — holds only this, and presenting it as a cookie is looked up as the hash of
 * the hash, which names no row. A fast digest rather than a password KDF because the token is random,
 * not chosen by a person: the choice `google-oidc.ts` makes for its state.
 */
export function hashSessionToken(raw: string): string {
  return createHash("sha256").update(raw, "utf8").digest("hex");
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the second schema half**

`packages/identity/src/schema/sessions.ts` (final):

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { check, index, uniqueIndex } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
import { id, label, newId, nowIso, table, tsString } from "@waitron/db";

/**
 * A shift login: a person active at a physical till, keyed to the TILL. MUTABLE, with no append-only
 * trigger: `ended_at` is stamped on logout, and the callers end a session that way rather than
 * deleting it. The till's cookie carries a random token; this row stores only its hash
 * (`../session-token.ts`), so a copy of the database signs nobody in. `id` is the row's identity,
 * never the cookie — `authorize` takes it.
 */
export const sessions = table(
  "sessions",
  {
    id: id("id").primaryKey().$defaultFn(newId),
    tokenHash: label("token_hash").notNull(),
    // No foreign keys. The person comes back from `verifyPersonCredential` and the till from the
    // authenticated device's own registration (`apps/server/src/till-api.ts`, `device.tillId`); a
    // session whose person row is gone resolves as no session (`authorize.ts`, the inner join).
    personId: id("person_id").notNull(),
    tillId: id("till_id").notNull(),
    openedAt: tsString("opened_at").notNull().$defaultFn(nowIso),
    endedAt: tsString("ended_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    // The "open session at a till" lookup filters on till_id then ended_at IS NULL; this index
    // covers the equality predicate. Kept plain (not partial) so drizzle-kit round-trips it.
    index("sessions_open_idx").on(t.tillId),
    uniqueIndex("sessions_token_hash_uq").on(t.tokenHash),
    check("sessions_token_hash_ck", sql`length(${t.tokenHash}) = 64`),
  ],
);
```

callback. Docstring: replace its last sentence with "The dashboard cookie carries a random token; this

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement the lookups**

`packages/identity/src/login.ts`:

```ts
import { hashSessionToken, mintSessionToken } from "./session-token.js";

export interface Session {
  /** The row's identity — what `authorize` takes. Never the cookie. */
  id: string;
  /** The bearer token the shift cookie carries. Only its hash is stored. */
  token: string;
  // …personId, tillId, role, locale unchanged
}

export async function loginWithPin(
  tx: Transaction,
  input: { tillId: string; personId: string; pin: string },
): Promise<Session> {
  const { role, locale } = await verifyPersonCredential(tx, input.personId, input.pin);
  const token = mintSessionToken();
  const [row] = await tx
    .insert(sessions)
    .values({ personId: input.personId, tillId: input.tillId, tokenHash: hashSessionToken(token) })
    .returning({ id: sessions.id });
  return { id: row!.id, token, personId: input.personId, tillId: input.tillId, role, locale };
}

/** Ends the open session the cookie's `token` names. True if this call closed it; false if it was
 * already ended, or the token names no session — a row id or a stored hash names none. */
export async function endSession(tx: Transaction, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const updated = await tx
    .update(sessions)
    .set({ endedAt: nowIso() })
    .where(and(eq(sessions.tokenHash, hashSessionToken(token)), isNull(sessions.endedAt)))
    .returning({ id: sessions.id });
  return updated.length > 0;
}
```

```ts
import { hashSessionToken, mintSessionToken } from "./session-token.js";

export interface ManagementSession {
  /** The bearer token the dashboard cookie carries. Only its hash is stored. */
  token: string;
  personId: string;
}

export async function startManagementSession(
  tx: Transaction,
  input: { personId: string },
): Promise<ManagementSession> {
  const token = mintSessionToken();
  await tx
    .insert(managementSessions)
    .values({ personId: input.personId, tokenHash: hashSessionToken(token) });
  return { token, personId: input.personId };
}
```

```ts
import { hashSessionToken, sessions } from "@waitron/identity";

/** Writes the session's token into the shift cookie. `httpOnly` so no browser script can read it (the
 * token is a bearer credential); … (rest of the existing doc unchanged) */
export function setSessionCookie(c: Context, token: string, secure: boolean): void {
  setCookie(c, SESSION_COOKIE, token, { httpOnly: true, secure, sameSite: "Strict", path: "/" });
}

export async function requireSession(
  deps: { db: Database },
  c: Context,
): Promise<{ personId: string; sessionId: string }> {
  const token = readSessionId(c);
  if (token === null || !isUuid(token)) throw new AppError("session.required", {});
  const row = await withTransaction(deps.db, async (tx) => {
    const [found] = await tx
      .select({ id: sessions.id, personId: sessions.personId })
      .from(sessions)
      .where(and(eq(sessions.tokenHash, hashSessionToken(token)), isNull(sessions.endedAt)));
    return found ?? null;
  });
  if (row === null) throw new AppError("session.required", {});
  return { personId: row.personId, sessionId: row.id };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `apps/server/src/backup-config.ts`, add above `loadBackupConfig`:

```ts
/**
 * The operator's recovery key, read on its own: it locks the scheduled archive AND this box's state
 * row in the venue database (`sealed-state.ts`), and the second needs no archive destination.
 * Unset or empty is `undefined`; a key under `MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH` throws
 * `backup.recovery_key_too_short`, the same floor the archive has always had.
 */
export function loadRecoveryKey(env: Env): string | undefined {
  const recoveryKey = env.WAITRON_BACKUP_RECOVERY_KEY;
  if (isUnset(recoveryKey)) return undefined;
  if (recoveryKey.length < MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH) {
    throw new AppError("backup.recovery_key_too_short", { min: MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH });
  }
  return recoveryKey;
}
```

and replace the key block inside `loadBackupConfig` (the four lines from
`const recoveryKey = env.WAITRON_BACKUP_RECOVERY_KEY;` to the closing `}` of the length check) with:

```ts
  const recoveryKey = loadRecoveryKey(env);
  if (recoveryKey === undefined) throw new AppError("backup.recovery_key_missing", {});
```

The order of the two refusals is unchanged: destinations are parsed first, so a box with no
destination still gets `undefined` from `loadBackupConfig` whatever its key says.

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement**

In `apps/server/src/backup-env-writer.ts`, add `import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";` and,
below `writeBackupEnv`:

```ts
/**
 * Set the recovery key in `<stateDir>/backup.env`, keeping every other line the file holds — so a
 * box with no archive destination can hold a key for its locked state row, and a box with one keeps
 * its destination, schedule and retention. Round-trip guarded like `writeBackupEnv`, atomic, 0600.
 */
export async function writeRecoveryKey(
  stateDir: string,
  input: { recoveryKey: string; keyRotatedAt: string | undefined },
): Promise<void> {
  const path = join(stateDir, "backup.env");
  let existing: Record<string, string> = {};
  try {
    existing = parseEnvFile(await readFile(path, "utf8"));
  } catch (err) {
    if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw err;
  }
  const record: Record<string, string> = {
    ...existing,
    WAITRON_BACKUP_RECOVERY_KEY: input.recoveryKey,
  };
  if (input.keyRotatedAt !== undefined) record.WAITRON_BACKUP_KEY_ROTATED_AT = input.keyRotatedAt;
  assertStorableRecord(record);
  await writeFileAtomic(path, formatEnvFile(record), 0o600);
}
```

recovery kit carries the first. Read on 2026-09-23: today `apply` writes whatever key the body
carries (`backup-api.ts:235-256`), and the dashboard's archive wizard mints a fresh one on every
load of a box whose archives are off (`backup-screen.ts`, `#load` → `#mint` → `POST
/api/backup/mint-key`), so turning archives on after streaming would silently replace the kit's key.

```bash
The recovery key was only read when a backup folder was configured, so a box

files into the venue database with that key, and a venue that streams to a
bucket may never set up a backup folder at all.

writeRecoveryKey sets the key in backup.env and keeps the other settings. The
rotate route now changes the key of a box that has a key and no folder, and the
recovery-key route answers for such a box instead of saying null.

Turning archives on now reuses a key the box already holds, so a venue keeps
one recovery key: an apply that names a different key is refused with
```

```ts
// This box's own state files, locked with the recovery key, in one row of the venue database.
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { CORE_MIGRATIONS, withTransaction } from "@waitron/db";
import { useVenueDb } from "@waitron/db/testing/venue-db.js";
import type { ArchiveEntry } from "./backup-archive.js";
import type { BackupManifest } from "./backup-manifest.js";
import { ALL_MODULES } from "./modules.js";
import {
  collectSealedEntries,
  createSealedStateRefresher,
  readSealedStateRow,
  sealNodeState,
  unsealNodeState,
  type SealedStateDeps,
} from "./sealed-state.js";
import { RECOVERY_FILES } from "./state-secrets.js";

const suite = useVenueDb({ migrations: [CORE_MIGRATIONS] });

const KEY = "recovery-key-one-strong";
const OTHER_KEY = "recovery-key-two-different";
const NODE_ID = "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333";
const MANIFEST: BackupManifest = {
  manifestVersion: 1,
  createdAt: "2026-09-23T00:00:00.000Z",
  environment: "preproduction",
  modules: { core: 1 },
};
const REQUIRED = RECOVERY_FILES.map((rel) => `secrets/${rel}`);

let stateDir: string;
beforeEach(async () => {
  stateDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "sealed-state-"));
  for (const rel of RECOVERY_FILES) {
    await mkdir(join(stateDir, dirname(rel)), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(join(stateDir, rel), `${rel}-contents`);
  }
});
afterEach(async () => {
  await rm(stateDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

const names = (entries: ArchiveEntry[]) => entries.map((e) => e.name);
const text = (entries: ArchiveEntry[], name: string) =>
  Buffer.from(entries.find((e) => e.name === name)!.bytes).toString("utf8");

/** The code an AppError carries, or the thrown value itself when nothing was a code. */
function codeThrownBy(fn: () => unknown): unknown {
  try {
    fn();
  } catch (error) {
    return (error as { code?: unknown }).code ?? error;
  }
  return "nothing thrown";
}

const deps = (over: Partial<SealedStateDeps> = {}): SealedStateDeps => ({
  db: suite.db,
  nodeId: NODE_ID,
  stateDir,
  modules: ALL_MODULES,
  resolvers: {},
  environment: "preproduction",
  readRecoveryKey: async () => KEY,
  now: () => new Date("2026-09-23T10:00:00.000Z"),
  log: vi.fn(),
  ...over,
});

const row = () => withTransaction(suite.db, (tx) => readSealedStateRow(tx, NODE_ID));

describe("collectSealedEntries", () => {
  it("carries every archive entry except the database copy, in the archive's order", async () => {
    await writeFile(join(stateDir, "backup.env"), "WAITRON_BACKUP_RECOVERY_KEY=x\n");
    await writeFile(join(stateDir, "modules.json"), '{"modules":{}}\n');
    const entries = await collectSealedEntries({
      stateDir,
      modules: ALL_MODULES,
      resolvers: {},
      manifest: MANIFEST,
    });
    expect(names(entries)).toEqual([
      "manifest.json",
      ...REQUIRED,
      "secrets/backup.env",
      "secrets/modules.json",
    ]);
    expect(JSON.parse(text(entries, "manifest.json"))).toEqual(MANIFEST);
    expect(text(entries, "secrets/secrets.env")).toBe("secrets.env-contents");
  });
});

describe("sealNodeState / unsealNodeState", () => {
  const entries: ArchiveEntry[] = [
    { name: "manifest.json", bytes: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(MANIFEST)) },
    { name: "secrets/secrets.env", bytes: Buffer.from("WAITRON_CREDENTIALS_KEY=abc\n") },
  ];

  it("gives back the same entries under the key it was sealed with", () => {
    const opened = unsealNodeState(sealNodeState(entries, KEY), KEY);
    expect(names(opened)).toEqual(names(entries));
    expect(text(opened, "secrets/secrets.env")).toBe("WAITRON_CREDENTIALS_KEY=abc\n");
  });

  it("opens nothing under a different recovery key", () => {
    const sealed = sealNodeState(entries, KEY);
    expect(codeThrownBy(() => unsealNodeState(sealed, OTHER_KEY))).toBe(
      "recovery.passphrase_invalid",
    );
  });

  it("opens nothing once a byte of the sealed row has changed", () => {
    const sealed = Buffer.from(sealNodeState(entries, KEY));
    sealed[sealed.length - 1] ^= 0xff;
    expect(codeThrownBy(() => unsealNodeState(sealed, KEY))).toBe("recovery.passphrase_invalid");
  });

  it("does not carry the plaintext in the sealed bytes", () => {
    const sealed = Buffer.from(sealNodeState(entries, KEY));
    expect(sealed.includes(Buffer.from("WAITRON_CREDENTIALS_KEY"))).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("createSealedStateRefresher", () => {
  it("writes this node's row, which the key opens to the state files and a manifest read off the database", async () => {
    expect(await createSealedStateRefresher(deps()).refresh()).toBe("sealed");
    const entries = unsealNodeState((await row())!, KEY);
    expect(names(entries)).toEqual(["manifest.json", ...REQUIRED]);
    const manifest = JSON.parse(text(entries, "manifest.json")) as BackupManifest;
    expect(manifest.environment).toBe("preproduction");
    // Read off the migrated database, not a fixture: core is applied, so its version is above 0.
    expect(manifest.modules.core).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it("replaces the row rather than adding one, and carries each file as it now reads", async () => {
    const refresher = createSealedStateRefresher(deps());
    await refresher.refresh();
    await writeFile(join(stateDir, "modules.json"), '{"modules":{"fiscal-none":false}}\n');
    await refresher.refresh();
    const count = await suite.db.execute<{ n: number }>(
      sql`select count(*) as n from node_sealed_state`,
    );
    expect(count.rows[0]!.n).toBe(1);
    expect(text(unsealNodeState((await row())!, KEY), "secrets/modules.json")).toBe(
      '{"modules":{"fiscal-none":false}}\n',
    );
  });

  it("writes nothing when the box has no recovery key", async () => {
    const outcome = await createSealedStateRefresher(
      deps({ readRecoveryKey: async () => undefined }),
    ).refresh();
    expect(outcome).toBe("no_key");
    expect(await row()).toBeNull();
  });

  it("reports a missing state file by its code, never throws, and keeps the row it had", async () => {
    const log = vi.fn();
    const refresher = createSealedStateRefresher(deps({ log }));
    await refresher.refresh();
    await rm(join(stateDir, "secrets.env"));
    expect(await refresher.refresh()).toBe("failed");
    expect(log).toHaveBeenCalledWith("warn", "backup.sealed_state_failed", {
      errorCode: "recovery.state_incomplete",
    });
    // The earlier row is still there and still opens: a failed refresh must not blank it.
    expect(text(unsealNodeState((await row())!, KEY), "secrets/secrets.env")).toBe(
      "secrets.env-contents",
    );
  });

  it("runs one refresh at a time, so a slow refresh cannot land after a newer one", async () => {
    // The first refresh reads the OLD key and is held there; the second reads the new one. Run
    // side by side, the second would finish first and the first would then overwrite it with a row
    // only the old key opens — which the recovery kit would no longer hold.
    let releaseFirst!: () => void;
    const firstHeld = new Promise<void>((resolve) => (releaseFirst = resolve));
    let reads = 0;
    const refresher = createSealedStateRefresher(
      deps({
        readRecoveryKey: async () => {
          reads += 1;
          if (reads === 1) {
            await firstHeld;
            return KEY;
          }
          return OTHER_KEY;
        },
      }),
    );
    const first = refresher.refresh();
    const second = refresher.refresh();
    // Give the second every chance to finish on its own; queued behind the first, it cannot.
    await Promise.race([second, new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000))]);
    releaseFirst();
    await Promise.all([first, second]);
    const sealedNow = await row();
    // The row the last-called refresh wrote opens with the newer key.
    expect(codeThrownBy(() => unsealNodeState(sealedNow!, OTHER_KEY))).toBe("nothing thrown");
  }, 20_000);
});
```

and the 20 s bound leave room on a loaded CI runner.)

```ts
import { binary, id, table, ts } from "./columns.js";

/**
 * One row per node: everything the box's encrypted archive carries except the database copy — the
 * manifest, the state-folder secrets and settings — packed and locked with the operator's recovery
 * key (`apps/server/src/sealed-state.ts`). It lives in the venue database so it travels wherever
 * the database is copied, and it opens only with the recovery key.
 *
 * `node_id` names no foreign key: a `local` table may not reference a `state` one
 * (`scripts/two-file-foreign-keys.test.ts`), and the writer takes the id from the box's own trading
 * configuration rather than from a row.
 */
export const nodeSealedState = table("node_sealed_state", {
  nodeId: id("node_id").primaryKey().notNull(),
  sealed: binary("sealed").notNull(),
  updatedAt: ts("updated_at").notNull(),
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Share the archive's entry assembly**

Create `apps/server/src/archive-entries.ts`:

```ts
import type { WaitronModule } from "@waitron/module";
import type { ArchiveEntry } from "./backup-archive.js";
import type { BackupManifest } from "./backup-manifest.js";
import { OPTIONAL_BACKUP_STATE, collectOptionalStateFiles } from "./backup-optional-state.js";
import { collectModuleNonDbState } from "./backup-sources.js";
import { collectStateSecrets } from "./state-secrets.js";

/** Everything a backup archive carries besides its manifest and the database copy, read off disk. */
export interface StateParts {
  readonly nonDbState: ArchiveEntry[];
  readonly secrets: Record<string, string>;
  readonly optionalState: Record<string, string>;
}

/**
 * Read the three collections concurrently. A missing `RECOVERY_FILES` path throws
 * `recovery.state_incomplete`; a missing optional file is skipped (`backup-optional-state.ts`).
 */
export async function collectStateParts(deps: {
  readonly stateDir: string;
  readonly modules: readonly WaitronModule[];
  readonly resolvers: Record<string, string>;
}): Promise<StateParts> {
  const [secrets, nonDbState, optionalState] = await Promise.all([
    collectStateSecrets(deps.stateDir),
    collectModuleNonDbState(deps.modules, deps.resolvers),
    collectOptionalStateFiles(deps.stateDir, OPTIONAL_BACKUP_STATE),
  ]);
  return { nonDbState, secrets, optionalState };
}

/**
 * The archive's entries in their one fixed order: the manifest, the database copy when there is
 * one, module state as `<source>/<file>`, then `secrets/<path>` for the required files and the
 * optional ones. The locked state row is this list with `dump` null (`sealed-state.ts`); the
 * restore writes every `secrets/` entry back under the state folder (`restore.ts`).
 */
export function assembleArchiveEntries(
  manifest: BackupManifest,
  dump: Uint8Array | null,
  parts: StateParts,
): ArchiveEntry[] {
  return [
    { name: "manifest.json", bytes: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(manifest)) },
    ...(dump === null ? [] : [{ name: "db.dump", bytes: dump }]),
    ...parts.nonDbState,
    ...Object.entries(parts.secrets).map(([path, contents]) => ({
      name: `secrets/${path}`,
      bytes: Buffer.from(contents),
    })),
    ...Object.entries(parts.optionalState).map(([name, contents]) => ({
      name: `secrets/${name}`,
      bytes: Buffer.from(contents),
    })),
  ];
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Implement the sealed state**

Create `apps/server/src/sealed-state.ts`:

```ts
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { nodeSealedState, withTransaction, type Database, type Transaction } from "@waitron/db";
import type { WaitronModule } from "@waitron/module";
import { codeOf } from "@waitron/server-kit";
import { assembleArchiveEntries, collectStateParts } from "./archive-entries.js";
import { decryptArtifact, encryptArtifact } from "./artifact-cipher.js";
import { packArchive, unpackArchive, type ArchiveEntry } from "./backup-archive.js";
import { buildManifest, type BackupManifest } from "./backup-manifest.js";
import type { DeploymentEnvironment } from "./config.js";
import type { Logger } from "./logger.js";

/** The archive's entries without the database copy, in the archive's order. */
export async function collectSealedEntries(deps: {
  readonly stateDir: string;
  readonly modules: readonly WaitronModule[];
  readonly resolvers: Record<string, string>;
  readonly manifest: BackupManifest;
}): Promise<ArchiveEntry[]> {
  return assembleArchiveEntries(deps.manifest, null, await collectStateParts(deps));
}

/** Packed and locked exactly as an archive is, so one key and one reader open both. */
export function sealNodeState(entries: ArchiveEntry[], recoveryKey: string): Uint8Array {
  return encryptArtifact(packArchive(entries), recoveryKey);
}

/** Throws `recovery.passphrase_invalid` for a wrong key or altered bytes (`artifact-cipher.ts`). */
export function unsealNodeState(sealed: Uint8Array, recoveryKey: string): ArchiveEntry[] {
  return unpackArchive(decryptArtifact(sealed, recoveryKey));
}

export async function writeSealedStateRow(
  tx: Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
  sealed: Uint8Array,
  at: Date,
): Promise<void> {
  await tx
    .insert(nodeSealedState)
    .values({ nodeId, sealed, updatedAt: at })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: nodeSealedState.nodeId, set: { sealed, updatedAt: at } });
}

export async function readSealedStateRow(
  tx: Transaction,
  nodeId: string,
): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
  const rows = await tx
    .select({ sealed: nodeSealedState.sealed })
    .from(nodeSealedState)
    .where(eq(nodeSealedState.nodeId, nodeId));
  return rows[0]?.sealed ?? null;
}

export type SealedStateOutcome = "sealed" | "no_key" | "failed";

export interface SealedStateDeps {
  readonly db: Database;
  /** This machine's own node id — `config.till.nodeId`. */
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly stateDir: string;
  readonly modules: readonly WaitronModule[];
  readonly resolvers: Record<string, string>;
  readonly environment: DeploymentEnvironment;
  /** Read afresh on every refresh, so a rotated key locks the next row. */
  readonly readRecoveryKey: () => Promise<string | undefined>;
  readonly now: () => Date;
  readonly log: Logger;
}

export interface SealedStateRefresher {
  refresh(): Promise<SealedStateOutcome>;
}

/**
 * Re-reads the state files and the key and rewrites this node's row.
 *
 * Refreshes run one at a time, in call order. Each reads the key and the files when it starts, so
 * the last one called writes the last row; run side by side, a refresh holding an older key could
 * land after a newer one, leaving a row only a superseded key opens.
 *
 * It never throws. A failure is logged as `backup.sealed_state_failed` with its code and the
 * previous row is left as it was: the box keeps trading without a fresh row, as it keeps trading
 * when a backup tick fails (`backup-supervisor.ts`).
 */
export function createSealedStateRefresher(deps: SealedStateDeps): SealedStateRefresher {
  const once = async (): Promise<SealedStateOutcome> => {
    try {
      const recoveryKey = await deps.readRecoveryKey();
      if (recoveryKey === undefined) {
        deps.log("info", "backup.sealed_state_skipped", { reason: "no_recovery_key" });
        return "no_key";
      }
      const now = deps.now();
      const manifest = await buildManifest({
        db: deps.db,
        modules: deps.modules,
        environment: deps.environment,
        now,
      });
      const entries = await collectSealedEntries({
        stateDir: deps.stateDir,
        modules: deps.modules,
        resolvers: deps.resolvers,
        manifest,
      });
      // The key derivation is outside the transaction: it is the slow part, and the write lock
      // must not wait on it.
      const sealed = sealNodeState(entries, recoveryKey);
      await withTransaction(deps.db, (tx) => writeSealedStateRow(tx, deps.nodeId, sealed, now));
      deps.log("info", "backup.sealed_state_refreshed", { entries: entries.length });
      return "sealed";
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log("warn", "backup.sealed_state_failed", { errorCode: codeOf(err) });
      return "failed";
    }
  };
  let tail: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
  return {
    refresh: () => {
      const next = tail.then(once);
      tail = next;
      return next;
    },
  };
}
```

```bash
reference a state one. It is left out of the dashboard's change feed.
```

### Task 3a: One process per venue folder

**Branch:** `feat/sqlite-slice2-venue-lock`

**What the lock is, and why this mechanism.** A second process opening the same venue folder is
refused; opens inside one process share the lock; and a process that dies holding it does not
leave the folder locked — the property that matters most, because a stale lock would stop the box
from starting. The lock is a SQLite transaction (`begin immediate`) held on an otherwise empty file,
`venue.lock`, for as long as any open in the process is using the folder. It is the same mechanism
the migrator already uses (`packages/migrations/src/apply.ts`, `migrations.lock`), whose comment
records that a lock FILE created exclusively would survive a crash and "wedge every later boot".
Measured again for this plan, 2026-09-23, Node v26.7.0 (`node:sqlite`), macOS, by two probe
scripts kept in the session scratchpad (`scratchpad/lockprobe/probe.mjs`, `probe2.mjs`; the
conventions-data receipt in Step 15 restates what each printed so it does not depend on them):

- while one process held `begin immediate` on the file, another process's `begin immediate` with a
  zero busy timeout was refused errcode 5, `database is locked`, in under a millisecond; a plain
  read of the file from a third connection was not blocked;
- a second connection in the SAME process was refused the same way (errcode 5) — which is why the
  lock is counted per process instead of taken per open;
- after the holder was killed with `SIGKILL`, a new acquirer succeeded at once, with the dead
  holder's 512-byte `venue.lock-journal` still on disk; after a clean close only `venue.lock` remains;
- closing the connection with the transaction still open released it.

That is macOS. The box runs Linux; the store suite's `SIGKILL` case below runs in CI on Linux, and
that run is the Linux measurement. Nobody may unlink `venue.lock` while it is held: unlinking is what
`db-wipe.ts` records defeats the migrations lock the same way.

**Why the migrator's lock cannot serve.** It is held only while migrations run, then released; and
it WAITS (up to two minutes, `LOCK_WAIT_MS`) for another migrator, where a second server must be
refused at once. Holding it for the life of the process would make that process's own later migrate
— the cold restore and `waitron-rejoin` migrate in-process — wait on itself: a second connection in
one process is refused (measured above). So the migrator keeps its lock, and `venue.lock` is a
second file with a different lifetime. They nest without conflict: `applyMigrations` takes
`migrations.lock`, then opens the store, which takes `venue.lock`.

**Every caller, and what it does now** (from `grep -rn "openVenueStore\|openVenueDatabase"`, 2026-09-23):

| Caller | Runs | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/server/src/boot.ts` (stamp probe line 836, long-lived store line 868) | the server | locks (default); the long-lived store holds it for the process's life |
| `apps/server/src/backup-supervisor.ts` (`reload`) | inside the server | shares the server's lock |
| `apps/server/src/node-entry.ts` (`assertNotAhead`) and the staged restore it runs | the container entrypoint, same process as the server | locks, sequentially, before the server opens |
| `apps/server/src/restore.ts` (`writeValidated`, hooks via `openVenue`) | `waitron-restore` (server stopped) and the staged restore | takes the lock BEFORE replacing `venue.db`, held to the end; refused while a server runs |
| `apps/server/src/rejoin-command.ts` | `waitron-rejoin` (server stopped) | takes the lock before its first read, held through the wipe and re-migrate; refused while a server runs |
| `packages/migrations/src/apply.ts` | boot, restore, rejoin, dev scripts | locks (default), inside its own `migrations.lock` |
| `packages/provisioning/src/bin.ts` (`waitron-provision venue`) | once per venue | locks; refused while a server runs, printed as `provisioning.database_in_use {…}` |
| `apps/server/scripts/register-till.ts` | closes a node's chain | locks; refused while a server runs (header gains a line saying so) |
| `apps/server/scripts/dev-setup.ts`, `dev-onboard` via `applyMigrations` | before a dev server starts | locks; refused while a dev server runs. Only one dev server runs at a time: the dev ports are fixed, and `wa-wt` stops the running instance and waits for its process group before a switch (`~/workspace/tools/wa-wt`, read, lines 302–345). `tsx watch` waits for the old process's `exit` before starting the new one (`killProcess` in `node_modules/.pnpm/tsx@4.23.13/node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs`, read) |
| `apps/server/src/break-glass-command.ts` | documented to run beside the server (`deploy/README.md`) | `exclusive: false` — no lock |
| `packages/credentials/src/bin.ts` | documented to run beside the server (`apps/server/README.md`) | `exclusive: false` — no lock |
| `apps/server/scripts/record-one-sale.ts`, `settle-invoice-first.ts` | write sales for a running server to drain | `exclusive: false` — no lock |
| `apps/server/src/fiscal-readiness-runner.ts` | its own separate directory | locks its own directory; no contention |
| `*-demo.ts` scripts, `scripts/testing/venue.ts`, `useVenueDb` | their own temporary directories | locks; no contention |
