Create `apps/server/src/testing/s3-test-server.ts`:

```ts
import { execFile, spawn, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createConnection, createServer, type AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { isUnset } from "../env-value.js";

// versitygw run as a plain child process: the S3-compatible server the stream loop test streams to.
// No package suite may start a container (CLAUDE.md §4). Why versitygw, and the measurements behind
// the flags below, are in docs/developers/testing-guide.md → "The stream loop test".

/** Must equal `VERSITYGW_VERSION` in `scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs`; that script's suite reads this line. */
export const VERSITYGW_VERSION = "1.8.0";

const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../../", import.meta.url));

/** Where `node scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs` installs it. `WAITRON_VERSITYGW_BIN` overrides. */
export const DEFAULT_VERSITYGW_BIN = join(REPO_ROOT, ".bin", "versitygw");

const ACCESS_KEY_ID = "waitronlooptest";
const SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = "waitron-loop-test-secret";
/** At least three characters: versitygw refuses shorter names with `InvalidBucketName`. */
const BUCKET = "waitron-loop";
const READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;
const STOP_GRACE_MS = 5_000;
const VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

export type BinaryLookup = { ok: true; bin: string } | { ok: false; reason: string };

export interface S3TestServer {
  endpoint: string;
  region: string;
  bucket: string;
  accessKeyId: string;
  secretAccessKey: string;
  /** The last 8 KiB the server printed, for a failure message. */
  log(): string;
  /** SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period; resolves once the process is gone either way. */
  stop(): Promise<void>;
  /** Freezes the process (SIGSTOP): every call to it then hangs, answering nothing. */
  pause(): void;
  /** Lets a paused process run again (SIGCONT). */
  resume(): void;
}

/** The pinned versitygw, or why it is not usable here. Never throws. */
export async function resolveVersitygw(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<BinaryLookup> {
  const bin = isUnset(env.WAITRON_VERSITYGW_BIN) ? DEFAULT_VERSITYGW_BIN : env.WAITRON_VERSITYGW_BIN;
  try {
    const { stdout } = await promisify(execFile)(bin, ["--version"], {
      timeout: VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS,
    });
    const version = /^Version\s*:\s*(\S+)\s*$/m.exec(stdout)?.[1];
    if (version !== VERSITYGW_VERSION) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        reason: `${bin} reports versitygw ${version ?? "(no version line)"}, not the pinned ${VERSITYGW_VERSION}`,
      };
    }
    return { ok: true, bin };
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `versitygw is not runnable at ${bin}: ${(error as Error).message}` };
  }
}

/** Live servers, killed if the test process exits before a suite's teardown runs. */
const live = new Set<ChildProcess>();
process.once("exit", () => {
  for (const child of live) child.kill("SIGKILL");
});

/**
 * Start versitygw on an OS-chosen loopback port, serving one bucket from a directory under `root`.
 * `--sidecar` keeps object metadata in a plain directory rather than in extended attributes, so the
 * server does not depend on what the temporary filesystem supports. A directory under the gateway
 * root IS a bucket, so the bucket is made with `mkdir` and no S3 call.
 */
export async function startS3TestServer(opts: { bin: string; root: string }): Promise<S3TestServer> {
  const data = join(opts.root, "data");
  const meta = join(opts.root, "meta");
  await mkdir(join(data, BUCKET), { recursive: true });
  await mkdir(meta, { recursive: true });
  const port = await freePort();

  const child = spawn(
    opts.bin,
    [
      "--access",
      ACCESS_KEY_ID,
      "--secret",
      SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
      "--port",
      `127.0.0.1:${port}`,
      "posix",
      "--sidecar",
      meta,
      data,
    ],
    { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] },
  );
  live.add(child);

  let log = "";
  const collect = (chunk: Buffer): void => {
    log = (log + chunk.toString()).slice(-8192);
  };
  child.stdout?.on("data", collect);
  child.stderr?.on("data", collect);

  let exitCode: number | null | undefined;
  const exited = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    const settle = (code: number | null): void => {
      exitCode = code;
      live.delete(child);
      resolve();
    };
    child.once("exit", settle);
    child.once("error", () => settle(null));
  });

  const server: S3TestServer = {
    endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
    region: "us-east-1",
    bucket: BUCKET,
    accessKeyId: ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    secretAccessKey: SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    log: () => log,
    pause() {
      if (exitCode === undefined) child.kill("SIGSTOP");
    },
    resume() {
      if (exitCode === undefined) child.kill("SIGCONT");
    },
    async stop() {
      if (exitCode !== undefined) return;
      child.kill("SIGCONT"); // a paused process cannot act on SIGTERM
      child.kill("SIGTERM");
      const grace = new Promise<"late">((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve("late"), STOP_GRACE_MS));
      if ((await Promise.race([exited.then(() => "gone" as const), grace])) === "late") {
        child.kill("SIGKILL");
        child.stdout?.destroy();
        child.stderr?.destroy();
        await exited;
      }
    },
  };

  const deadline = Date.now() + READY_TIMEOUT_MS;
  try {
    for (;;) {
      if (exitCode !== undefined) {
        throw new Error(`versitygw exited with ${exitCode} before listening on ${port}: ${log}`);
      }
      if (await accepts(port)) return server;
      if (Date.now() >= deadline) {
        throw new Error(`versitygw did not listen on 127.0.0.1:${port} within ${READY_TIMEOUT_MS}ms: ${log}`);
      }
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
    }
  } catch (error) {
    await server.stop();
    throw error;
  }
}

function accepts(port: number): Promise<boolean> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const socket = createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port });
    socket.once("connect", () => {
      socket.destroy();
      resolve(true);
    });
    socket.once("error", () => {
      socket.destroy();
      resolve(false);
    });
  });
}

/** An OS-assigned port, released before use — the same shape as `boot.test.ts`'s `freePort`. */
function freePort(): Promise<number> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const probe = createServer();
    probe.once("error", reject);
    probe.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const { port } = probe.address() as AddressInfo;
      probe.close((error) => (error ? reject(error) : resolve(port)));
    });
  });
}
```

Create `apps/server/src/stream-loop.e2e.test.ts`:

```ts
// The slice-2 loop, end to end, with the real pinned Litestream and a real S3-compatible server:
//   - box A streams its venue to a bucket;
//   - A dies;
//   - box B is rebuilt from the bucket with nothing but the recovery kit;
//   - B sells under a fresh installation number and chain;
//   - B streams into a generation of its own and moves the pointer;
//   - a restore of B's generation holds exactly what B's database holds.
//
// The server is versitygw, run as a plain child process (`./testing/s3-test-server.ts`). Install both
// binaries with `node scripts/setup-litestream.mjs && node scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs`. Without
// them this case is reported SKIPPED, with the reason in its note. With CI=true (GitHub sets it on
// every job) or WAITRON_REQUIRE_STREAM_BINARIES=1, a missing binary FAILS the case instead.
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { X509Certificate } from "node:crypto";
import { copyFile, cp, mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createServer, type AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
import { connect as tlsConnect } from "node:tls";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { loadKeyRing, putCredential } from "@waitron/credentials";
import { nodeSealedState, nodes, openVenueDatabase, stampDeployment, withTransaction } from "@waitron/db";
import {
  installationFloor,
  registroSif,
  registrosFacturacion,
} from "@waitron/fiscal-verifactu";
import { hashPassword, hashPin } from "@waitron/identity";
import { applyMigrations, manifestSets, migrationOptionsFor } from "@waitron/migrations";
import { applyVenue, planVenue, quoteIdent } from "@waitron/provisioning";
import {
  LITESTREAM_VERSION,
  createS3ObjectStore,
  encodeRecoveryKit,
  probeBucket,
  readPointer,
  restoreGeneration,
  venuePrefix,
  verifyPointer,
  type BucketConfig,
  type ObjectStore,
} from "@waitron/stream";
import { recordOneSale } from "../scripts/record-one-sale.js";
import { startServer, type StartedServer } from "./boot.js";
import { loadBoxEnv } from "./box-env.js";
import { ensureBoxSecrets } from "./box-secrets.js";
import { formatEnvFile, parseEnvFile } from "./env-file.js";
import { isUnset } from "./env-value.js";
import { seedTermZeroMembership } from "./membership-seed.js";
import { ALL_MODULES } from "./modules.js";
import { establishNodeIdentity } from "./node-identity.js";
import { runRestore } from "./restore-command.js";
import { unsealNodeState } from "./sealed-state.js";
import { streamSettingsPayload } from "./stream-host.js";
import {
  VERSITYGW_VERSION,
  resolveVersitygw,
  startS3TestServer,
  type BinaryLookup,
  type S3TestServer,
} from "./testing/s3-test-server.js";

const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../", import.meta.url));
const INSTALL = "node scripts/setup-litestream.mjs && node scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs";
const REQUIRED =
  process.env.CI === "true" || process.env.WAITRON_REQUIRE_STREAM_BINARIES === "1";

const RECOVERY_KEY = "stream-loop-e2e-recovery-key";
const LOCALE = "es-ES";

// Each wait's own bound. The case's timeout is their sum plus a share for the work nothing here
// bounds (boots, migrations, provisioning, closes), because Vitest's timer fails a healthy run that
// outlasts it (CLAUDE.md §4). An upload wait restores the generation once per poll, so it also gets
// one restore's worth on top.
const POINTER_WAIT_MS = 30_000;
const UPLOAD_WAIT_MS = 30_000;
/** Sales timed with the S3 server up, and again with it stopped (stage 8b). */
const TIMED_SALES = 10;
const RESTORE_MS = 30_000;
const REBUILD_MS = 120_000;
const BOOT_MS = 30_000;
const S3_READY_MS = 10_000;
const UNTIMED_MS = 60_000;
const POLL_MS = 500;
const LOOP_TIMEOUT_MS =
  S3_READY_MS +
  2 * BOOT_MS +
  2 * POINTER_WAIT_MS +
  3 * (UPLOAD_WAIT_MS + RESTORE_MS) +
  // Stage 8b: the two-second pause, and 2 × TIMED_SALES sales at the 1,000 ms bound each at worst.
  2_000 +
  2 * TIMED_SALES * 1_000 +
  REBUILD_MS +
  RESTORE_MS +
  UNTIMED_MS;

async function resolveLitestream(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<BinaryLookup> {
  const bin = isUnset(env.WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN)
    ? join(REPO_ROOT, ".bin", "litestream")
    : env.WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN;
  try {
    const { stdout } = await promisify(execFile)(bin, ["version"], { timeout: 10_000 });
    const version = stdout.trim();
    if (version !== LITESTREAM_VERSION) {
      return { ok: false, reason: `${bin} reports litestream ${version}, not the pinned ${LITESTREAM_VERSION}` };
    }
    return { ok: true, bin };
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `litestream is not runnable at ${bin}: ${(error as Error).message}` };
  }
}

const litestream = await resolveLitestream(process.env);
const versitygw = await resolveVersitygw(process.env);
const missing = [litestream, versitygw].flatMap((lookup) => (lookup.ok ? [] : [lookup.reason]));
if (missing.length > 0 && !REQUIRED) {
  console.warn(`stream loop test SKIPPED: ${missing.join("; ")}. Install with: ${INSTALL}`);
}

interface BoxDirs {
  root: string;
  state: string;
  venue: string;
}

async function boxDirs(parent: string, name: string): Promise<BoxDirs> {
  const root = join(parent, name);
  const dirs = { root, state: join(root, "state"), venue: join(root, "state", "venue") };
  await mkdir(dirs.venue, { recursive: true });
  return dirs;
}

function freePort(): Promise<number> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const probe = createServer();
    probe.once("error", reject);
    probe.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const { port } = probe.address() as AddressInfo;
      probe.close((error) => (error ? reject(error) : resolve(port)));
    });
  });
}

async function waitFor<T>(what: string, timeoutMs: number, probe: () => Promise<T | undefined>): Promise<T> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const value = await probe();
    if (value !== undefined) return value;
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms waiting for ${what}`);
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, POLL_MS));
  }
}

/** Keys in the bucket containing `fragment`, whether the store returns them with its prefix or without. */
async function keysContaining(store: ObjectStore, fragment: string): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await store.list("")).map(({ key }) => key).filter((key) => key.includes(fragment));
}

/** The one venue id with a pointer in this bucket, or undefined before any pointer exists. */
async function venueIdInBucket(store: ObjectStore): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  for (const key of await keysContaining(store, "venues/")) {
    const match = /(?:^|\/)venues\/([^/]+)\/current\.json$/.exec(key);
    if (match !== null) ids.add(match[1]!);
  }
  if (ids.size > 1) throw new Error(`expected one venue in the loop test's bucket, found ${[...ids].join(", ")}`);
  return [...ids][0];
}

/**
 * Every table's rows, serialised and sorted, keyed by table name. Litestream's own two tables are
 * left out: Litestream 0.5.17 adds `_litestream_seq` and `_litestream_lock` to the database it
 * streams (measured 2026-09-23), and their contents are its bookkeeping, not the venue's.
 */
function tableContents(path: string): Map<string, string[]> {
  const db = new DatabaseSync(path);
  try {
    const tables = db
      .prepare(
        `select name from sqlite_schema where type = 'table'
           and name not like 'sqlite\\_%' escape '\\' and name not like '\\_litestream\\_%' escape '\\'
         order by name`,
      )
      .all() as { name: string }[];
    const contents = new Map<string, string[]>();
    for (const { name } of tables) {
      const rows = db.prepare(`select * from ${quoteIdent(name)}`).all();
      contents.set(
        name,
        rows
          .map((row) =>
            JSON.stringify(row, (_key, value: unknown) =>
              value instanceof Uint8Array
                ? Buffer.from(value).toString("hex")
                : typeof value === "bigint"
                  ? value.toString()
                  : value,
            ),
          )
          .sort(),
      );
    }
    return contents;
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}

/** Names of the tables whose rows differ, or which only one side has. */
function differingTables(a: Map<string, string[]>, b: Map<string, string[]>): string[] {
  const names = new Set([...a.keys(), ...b.keys()]);
  return [...names]
    .filter((name) => JSON.stringify(a.get(name)) !== JSON.stringify(b.get(name)))
    .sort();
}

describe("the stream loop: stream, rebuild from the bucket, sell under a fresh chain, stream again", () => {
  let scratch: string | undefined;
  let s3: S3TestServer | undefined;
  let serverA: StartedServer | undefined;
  let serverB: StartedServer | undefined;

  afterAll(async () => {
    if (serverA !== undefined) await serverA.close();
    if (serverB !== undefined) await serverB.close();
    if (s3 !== undefined) await s3.stop();
    if (scratch !== undefined) await rm(scratch, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  it(
    "box A streams, dies, box B is rebuilt from the kit, sells on a fresh chain and moves the pointer; B's generation restores to B's database",
    async (ctx) => {
      if (!litestream.ok || !versitygw.ok) {
        if (REQUIRED) {
          throw new Error(`stream loop test cannot run: ${missing.join("; ")}. CI installs both with: ${INSTALL}`);
        }
        // `return` so TypeScript narrows both lookups below; `ctx.skip` throws either way.
        return ctx.skip(`${missing.join("; ")} — install with: ${INSTALL}`);
      }
      const litestreamBin = litestream.bin;

      scratch = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "waitron-stream-loop-"));
      const migrationsRoot = join(scratch, "migrations");
      const fromSource = migrationOptionsFor(manifestSets(), null);
      for (const [index, set] of manifestSets().entries()) {
        await cp(fromSource[index]!.migrationsFolder, join(migrationsRoot, set.name), { recursive: true });
      }

      // 1. The bucket, and the conditional write every pointer move depends on. A server that does not
      //    refuse a stale write fails HERE, with the probe's reason, before anything streams.
      s3 = await startS3TestServer({ bin: versitygw.bin, root: join(scratch, "s3") });
      const bucket: BucketConfig = {
        endpoint: s3.endpoint,
        region: s3.region,
        bucket: s3.bucket,
        prefix: "loop/",
        accessKeyId: s3.accessKeyId,
        secretAccessKey: s3.secretAccessKey,
      };
      const store = createS3ObjectStore(bucket);
      expect(
        await probeBucket(store),
        `versitygw ${VERSITYGW_VERSION} failed the conditional-write probe; see testing-guide.md → "The stream loop test". Server log: ${s3.log()}`,
      ).toEqual({ ok: true });

      // 2. Box A, provisioned the way a setup boot leaves a box: secrets and TLS in the state folder,
      //    a migrated and provisioned venue, a node key and a term-0 membership document, and streaming
      //    switched on with a recovery key.
      const dirsA = await boxDirs(scratch, "box-a");
      const portA = await freePort();
      await ensureBoxSecrets({
        stateDir: dirsA.state,
        hostnames: ["waitron.local", "localhost"],
        now: () => new Date(),
        listIpv4: () => [],
      });
      const ring = loadKeyRing(parseEnvFile(await readFile(join(dirsA.state, "secrets.env"), "utf8")));
      await applyMigrations(dirsA.venue, fromSource);
      const seeding = await openVenueDatabase(dirsA.venue);
      let a: { nodeId: string; tillId: string; seriesId: string; locationId: string; publicKey: string };
      try {
        await stampDeployment(seeding.venue, "preproduction");
        const venue = await applyVenue(
          planVenue(
            {
              country: "ES",
              taxId: "74000001K",
              legalName: "Stream Loop SL",
              location: {
                name: "Sala principal",
                fiscalTerritory: "ES-common",
                invoiceLocales: [LOCALE],
                operationDescription: "Venta en establecimiento",
                addressLine1: "Calle Mayor 1",
                addressLine2: null,
                postalCode: "28013",
                city: "Madrid",
                province: "Madrid",
                timeZone: "Europe/Madrid",
                dayCutover: "05:00",
              },
              tillName: "Caja 1",
              seriesCode: "A",
              rectificativeSeriesCode: "R",
              admin: {
                displayName: "Administradora",
                firstNames: "Test",
                lastNames: "Operator",
                pinHash: hashPin("1234"),
                passwordHash: hashPassword("dashPass123"),
                email: "owner@example.test",
              },
            },
            ALL_MODULES,
          ),
          { db: seeding.venue, modules: ALL_MODULES },
        );
        await establishNodeIdentity({ ownerDb: seeding.venue, ring }, venue.nodeId);
        await seedTermZeroMembership({ db: seeding.venue, ring }, venue.nodeId, `https://127.0.0.1:${portA}`);
        // Stored the way Task 8a's Save stores it: the venue is this node's location (N9).
        await withTransaction(seeding.venue, (tx) =>
          putCredential(tx, ring, {
            purpose: "backup.stream",
            value: streamSettingsPayload({ venueId: venue.locationId, bucket }),
          }),
        );
        const [row] = await seeding.venue
          .select({ publicKey: nodes.publicKey })
          .from(nodes)
          .where(eq(nodes.id, venue.nodeId));
        a = {
          nodeId: venue.nodeId,
          tillId: venue.tillId,
          seriesId: venue.seriesIds[0]!,
          locationId: venue.locationId,
          publicKey: row!.publicKey!,
        };
      } finally {
        await seeding.close();
      }
      await writeFile(
        join(dirsA.state, "trading.env"),
        formatEnvFile({
          WAITRON_TILL_TILL_ID: a.tillId,
          WAITRON_TILL_NODE_ID: a.nodeId,
          WAITRON_TILL_SERIES_ID: a.seriesId,
          WAITRON_TILL_LOCATION_ID: a.locationId,
          WAITRON_ENV: "preproduction",
        }),
      );
      await writeFile(join(dirsA.state, "backup.env"), formatEnvFile({ WAITRON_BACKUP_RECOVERY_KEY: RECOVERY_KEY }));
      await writeFile(join(dirsA.state, "modules.json"), JSON.stringify({ modules: { "fiscal-none": false } }));

      const bootEnv = (dirs: BoxDirs, port: number): NodeJS.ProcessEnv => ({
        WAITRON_STATE_DIR: dirs.state,
        WAITRON_VENUE_DIR: dirs.venue,
        WAITRON_MIGRATIONS_DIR: migrationsRoot,
        WAITRON_HTTP_PORT: String(port),
        WAITRON_HTTP_LANDING_PORT: "0",
        WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN: litestreamBin,
      });

      // 3. A boots, opens its generation and moves the pointer only after the first full copy landed.
      serverA = await startServer(await loadBoxEnv(bootEnv(dirsA, portA), dirsA.state));
      const venueId = await waitFor("a pointer in the bucket", POINTER_WAIT_MS, () => venueIdInBucket(store));
      const pointerA = await waitFor("the pointer to name box A's generation", POINTER_WAIT_MS, async () => {
        const read = await readPointer(store, venueId);
        return read !== null && read.pointer.body.nodeId === a.nodeId ? read : undefined;
      });
      expect(verifyPointer(pointerA.pointer, a.publicKey)).toBe(true);
      expect(pointerA.pointer.body).toMatchObject({ venueId, nodeId: a.nodeId, term: 0 });
      expect(pointerA.pointer.body.generation.startsWith(`gen-0-${a.nodeId}-`)).toBe(true);

      const saleInGeneration = async (generation: string, saleId: string): Promise<true | undefined> => {
        const out = join(await mkdtemp(join(scratch!, "probe-")), "venue.db");
        await restoreGeneration({ litestreamBin, bucket, venueId, generation, outPath: out });
        const db = new DatabaseSync(out);
        try {
          return db.prepare("select 1 as hit from sales where id = ?").get(saleId) === undefined ? undefined : true;
        } finally {
          db.close();
        }
      };

      // 4. A sells, and the sale is confirmed in the bucket by RESTORING it, not by counting files.
      const saleA = await recordOneSale(
        { tillId: a.tillId, nodeId: a.nodeId, seriesId: a.seriesId, description: "Café", baseAmount: "1.50", vatRate: "10.00" },
        { WAITRON_VENUE_DIR: dirsA.venue, WAITRON_ENV: "preproduction" },
      );
      await waitFor("box A's sale to reach A's generation", UPLOAD_WAIT_MS, () =>
        saleInGeneration(pointerA.pointer.body.generation, saleA.saleId),
      );

      // 5. A dies: its server stops and its whole folder is gone. The kit is all that is left.
      await serverA.close();
      serverA = undefined;
      const leafA = new X509Certificate(await readFile(join(dirsA.state, "tls", "server.crt"), "utf8"));
      await rm(dirsA.root, { recursive: true, force: true });
      const kitPath = join(scratch, "recovery-kit.txt");
      await writeFile(
        kitPath,
        encodeRecoveryKit({ version: 1, venueId, bucket, recoveryKey: RECOVERY_KEY, pointerSignerPublicKey: a.publicKey }),
      );

      // 6. B is rebuilt from the bucket through the command line. A changed within the last ten
      //    minutes, so the owner's confirmation that it is gone is required, and given.
      const dirsB = await boxDirs(scratch, "box-b");
      const portB = await freePort();
      const rebuildStartedAt = new Date();
      const said: string[] = [];
      const code = await runRestore({
        argv: ["restore", "--from-bucket", kitPath, "--confirm-old-box-gone", "--confirm-venue", "74000001K"],
        env: {
          WAITRON_STATE_DIR: dirsB.state,
          WAITRON_VENUE_DIR: dirsB.venue,
          WAITRON_MIGRATIONS_DIR: migrationsRoot,
          WAITRON_ENV: "preproduction",
          WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN: litestreamBin,
        },
        out: (line) => said.push(line),
      });
      expect(code, said.join("\n")).toBe(0);
      const tradingB = parseEnvFile(await readFile(join(dirsB.state, "trading.env"), "utf8"));
      expect(tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_NODE_ID).toBe(a.nodeId);
      expect(tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_SERIES_ID).not.toBe(a.seriesId);

      // 7. B's first start: a membership document one term higher, a generation of its own, and the
      //    pointer moved — still verifiable with the key the owner's kit carries.
      serverB = await startServer(await loadBoxEnv(bootEnv(dirsB, portB), dirsB.state));
      const pointerB = await waitFor("the pointer to move to box B's generation", POINTER_WAIT_MS, async () => {
        const read = await readPointer(store, venueId);
        return read !== null && read.pointer.body.generation !== pointerA.pointer.body.generation ? read : undefined;
      });
      expect(verifyPointer(pointerB.pointer, a.publicKey)).toBe(true);
      expect(pointerB.pointer.body).toMatchObject({ venueId, nodeId: a.nodeId, term: 1 });
      expect(pointerB.pointer.body.generation.startsWith(`gen-1-${a.nodeId}-`)).toBe(true);
      // The old generation is still there: moving the pointer deletes nothing inside the window.
      expect(
        await keysContaining(store, `${venuePrefix(venueId)}${pointerA.pointer.body.generation}/`),
      ).not.toHaveLength(0);
      // Task 9a: B serves a NEW leaf, signed by the authority A had, to a client that trusts only the
      // restored ca.crt. The dead box's leaf would also verify against that authority, so the served
      // certificate is compared with both files: it must be B's re-issued one, not A's.
      const caB = await readFile(join(dirsB.state, "tls", "ca.crt"), "utf8");
      const leafB = new X509Certificate(await readFile(join(dirsB.state, "tls", "server.crt"), "utf8"));
      expect(leafB.serialNumber).not.toBe(leafA.serialNumber);
      const served = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
        const socket = tlsConnect({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: portB, ca: caB, servername: "waitron.local" }, () => {
          const serial = socket.getPeerCertificate().serialNumber;
          socket.end();
          resolve(serial);
        });
        socket.once("error", reject);
      });
      expect(served.toUpperCase()).toBe(leafB.serialNumber.toUpperCase());
      // Task 2b's refresh runs after Task 9a's re-issue in the same start, so the row B sealed carries
      // B's leaf, not A's.
      const sealedB = await openVenueDatabase(dirsB.venue);
      try {
        const [row] = await sealedB.venue
          .select({ sealed: nodeSealedState.sealed })
          .from(nodeSealedState)
          .where(eq(nodeSealedState.nodeId, a.nodeId));
        const leafInRow = unsealNodeState(row!.sealed, RECOVERY_KEY).find(
          (entry) => entry.name === "secrets/tls/server.crt",
        );
        expect(new X509Certificate(Buffer.from(leafInRow!.bytes)).serialNumber).toBe(leafB.serialNumber);
      } finally {
        await sealedB.close();
      }

      // 8. B sells on the series the restore opened, and the sale reaches B's generation.
      const saleB = await recordOneSale(
        {
          tillId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_TILL_ID!,
          nodeId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_NODE_ID!,
          seriesId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_SERIES_ID!,
          description: "Agua",
          baseAmount: "2.00",
          vatRate: "10.00",
        },
        { WAITRON_VENUE_DIR: dirsB.venue, WAITRON_ENV: "preproduction" },
      );
      await waitFor("box B's sale to reach B's generation", UPLOAD_WAIT_MS, () =>
        saleInGeneration(pointerB.pointer.body.generation, saleB.saleId),
      );

      // 8b. Sales keep their normal time with the S3 server stopped — spec §8.2, against the real
      //     Litestream (Task 7's stream-host case uses a fake one and cannot show this). The server is
      //     frozen with SIGSTOP, so every bucket call hangs rather than being refused. A sale that
      //     waited on the bucket would hang with it, or take the S3 client's own timeout of seconds;
      //     the bound sits far below that and far above a healthy sale.
      const idsB = {
        tillId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_TILL_ID!,
        nodeId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_NODE_ID!,
        seriesId: tradingB.WAITRON_TILL_SERIES_ID!,
      };
      const timedSale = async (i: number): Promise<{ ms: number; saleId: string }> => {
        const started = performance.now();
        const sale = await recordOneSale(
          { ...idsB, description: `Pan ${i}`, baseAmount: "1.00", vatRate: "10.00" },
          { WAITRON_VENUE_DIR: dirsB.venue, WAITRON_ENV: "preproduction" },
        );
        return { ms: performance.now() - started, saleId: sale.saleId };
      };
      const baseline: number[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < TIMED_SALES; i += 1) baseline.push((await timedSale(i)).ms);
      s3.pause();
      let lastSaleId = "";
      try {
        // Long enough for Litestream to be part-way through calls the server will not answer.
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2_000));
        const stopped: number[] = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < TIMED_SALES; i += 1) {
          const sale = await timedSale(TIMED_SALES + i);
          stopped.push(sale.ms);
          lastSaleId = sale.saleId;
        }
        expect(Math.max(...stopped)).toBeLessThan(Math.max(1_000, 5 * Math.max(...baseline)));
      } finally {
        s3.resume();
      }
      await waitFor("the sales made while the bucket was stopped to reach B's generation", UPLOAD_WAIT_MS, () =>
        saleInGeneration(pointerB.pointer.body.generation, lastSaleId),
      );

      // 9. B stops cleanly; a restore of its generation holds exactly what its database holds.
      await serverB.close();
      serverB = undefined;
      const restoredB = join(await mkdtemp(join(scratch, "restored-b-")), "venue.db");
      await restoreGeneration({
        litestreamBin,
        bucket,
        venueId,
        generation: pointerB.pointer.body.generation,
        outPath: restoredB,
      });
      const live = tableContents(join(dirsB.venue, "venue.db"));
      expect(differingTables(live, tableContents(restoredB))).toEqual([]);
      // The comparison can see a difference: one extra table in a copy is reported, by name.
      const control = join(dirname(restoredB), "control.db");
      await copyFile(restoredB, control);
      const controlDb = new DatabaseSync(control);
      try {
        controlDb.exec("create table loop_control (x)");
      } finally {
        controlDb.close();
      }
      expect(differingTables(live, tableContents(control))).toEqual(["loop_control"]);

      // 10. A's sale is on the old installation; B's is the first record of a fresh one.
      const readB = await openVenueDatabase(dirsB.venue);
      try {
        const sifs = await readB.venue
          .select({
            id: registroSif.id,
            numeroInstalacion: registroSif.numeroInstalacion,
            revocadoEn: registroSif.revocadoEn,
          })
          .from(registroSif)
          .where(eq(registroSif.nodeId, a.nodeId))
          .orderBy(registroSif.numeroInstalacion);
        expect(sifs).toHaveLength(2);
        const [old, fresh] = sifs;
        expect(old!.revocadoEn).not.toBeNull();
        expect(fresh!.revocadoEn).toBeNull();
        expect(fresh!.numeroInstalacion).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(
          installationFloor(new Date(rebuildStartedAt.getTime() - 60_000)),
        );
        const records = await readB.venue
          .select({
            saleId: registrosFacturacion.saleId,
            sifId: registrosFacturacion.sifId,
            primerRegistro: registrosFacturacion.primerRegistro,
          })
          .from(registrosFacturacion);
        expect(records).toHaveLength(2 + 2 * TIMED_SALES); // A's, B's, and stage 8b's
        expect(records).toEqual(
          expect.arrayContaining([
            { saleId: saleA.saleId, sifId: old!.id, primerRegistro: true },
            { saleId: saleB.saleId, sifId: fresh!.id, primerRegistro: true },
          ]),
        );
      } finally {
        await readB.close();
      }
    },
    LOOP_TIMEOUT_MS,
  );
});
```

- §2.1: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** Superseded: every table stays in `venue.db` and streams. A row

- §2.2: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** A generation's name also carries when it was opened —
  `gen-<term>-<node-id>-<opened-at, UTC>` — and opening one starts with a create-only write of a
  marker object inside it. A slice-2 rebuild reuses the dead box's node id, and without the time it
  could sign the same term into a folder that already exists. The pointer, not the name, says which
  generation is live. [Slice-2 spec §4.4](2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).

  Task 4 recorded `RESTART_RESYNCS` in the results note. If it is `false`, append: "After every
  pause the supervisor opens a new generation. The name gains no counter: its opening time and the
  create-only marker already keep two openings apart (Tasks 5 and 6)."
- §7.1: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** Slice 2 sets one full copy a day and 168 hours' (seven days')
  retention, not hourly copies and 30 days. Litestream's retention is set in hours only, and restoring
  to the latest point is exact whatever the full-copy interval. Which older restore points survive the
  window is measured in the [results note](../../research/2026-09-16-sqlite-failover-prototype.md)'s
  slice-2 section. [Slice-2 spec §4.4](2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).
- §7.3: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** The stream goes to S3-compatible buckets only. Litestream 0.5
  cannot encrypt what it uploads, so a NAS folder or a USB disk would hold the venue's whole database
  in the clear; the encrypted archive stays the way to put a copy on a USB disk.
  [Slice-2 spec §0](2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).
- §7.5: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** Slice 2's rebuild from the bucket claims no seat; seats arrive
  with promotion in slice 3. It resumes the dead node's own identity from a row locked with the
  recovery key that streams with the database, and the fiscal restore hook mints a fresh installation
  number, series and chain exactly as an archive restore does. [Slice-2 spec §3.1 and
  §5](2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).
- §7.7: > **Pointer, DATE (slice 2).** Freshness is read from the bucket: the age of the oldest change
  not yet there, found by listing the live generation about once a minute. It is not read from
  Litestream's own status, which would look healthy while Litestream wrote somewhere else. It shows on
  `/health` (which it never fails), the box status page and the dashboard alerts ALERT_CODES.
  [Slice-2 spec §7](2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md).

- New section, after *`TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` is required locally, for the `bench/`

  > ## The stream loop test
  >
  > `apps/server/src/stream-loop.e2e.test.ts` runs slice 2 end to end with the real pinned Litestream
  > and a real S3-compatible server started as a plain child process (no package suite starts a
  > container): stream, rebuild from the bucket, sell under a fresh chain, stream into the rebuilt
  > box's own generation, and compare a restore of that generation with the box's database.
  >
  > **Binaries.** `node scripts/setup-litestream.mjs && node scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs`
  > installs both under `.bin/` at the repository root; `WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN` and
  > `WAITRON_VERSITYGW_BIN` point elsewhere. A missing or wrong-version binary SKIPS the case locally,
  > with the reason in a console warning, and FAILS it when `CI=true` or
  > `WAITRON_REQUIRE_STREAM_BINARIES=1`.
  >
  > **Why versitygw 1.8.0.** Five candidates were run on 2026-09-23 with the same probe: a write "only
  > if absent" over an existing key, a write "only if unchanged" with a stale ETag, and twenty parallel
  > create-only writes. versitygw, SeaweedFS 4.47 and MinIO's last binary release all refused both
  > (412) and let one writer of twenty win. rclone `serve s3` overwrote the object both times. Garage
  > does not support the conditional write; its issue #1052 is open, and a maintainer wrote that
  > "adding this to Garage is not possible with our weak-consistency replication model". versitygw was
  > preferred: it answers `If-Match` on a missing key with 404 as AWS documents (SeaweedFS answers
  > 412), it is one process on one port, and its release publishes SHA-256 checksums (SeaweedFS
  > publishes MD5). MinIO's repository is archived and its community binaries are no longer published.
  >
  > **It runs with `--sidecar`**, which keeps object metadata in a plain directory instead of
  > extended attributes, so it does not depend on the temporary filesystem. Litestream 0.5.17
  > replicated to it and restored from it in both modes on darwin/arm64. Its first run on Linux is the
  > CI run that introduced it.
  >
  > **If the conditional-write probe fails** — the case's first assertion, which prints the probe's
  > reason and the server's log — the server is the suspect, not the product. Check
  > `.bin/versitygw --version`. The recorded fallback is SeaweedFS 4.47, whose run passed the same
  > probe; weigh its MD5-only checksums, eleven listening ports and three-second stop before
  > swapping.

**`docs/developers/ci-and-gates.md`**, a new subsection at the end of *CI job layout and scheduling*:
> ### `test-server`'s shards download two binaries for the stream loop test
>
> Each of the three `test-server` shards runs `node scripts/setup-litestream.mjs` and
> `node scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs` before its tests, because file sharding decides which shard
> gets `apps/server/src/stream-loop.e2e.test.ts`. That is 13,540,484 bytes of Litestream and
> 27,542,985 bytes of versitygw per shard, from GitHub's release downloads, each checked against a
> pinned SHA-256; the time it adds has not been measured. They are not cached: on 2026-09-23 the
> repository's Actions cache held 10.93 GB across 907 entries, about 9.6 GB of it Docker layers,
> and a new entry would compete under least-recently-used eviction with the pnpm store (7 entries,
> about 766 MB) and the Playwright browser (about 284 MB) that the test jobs restore. A GitHub release
> outage fails these shards, and the failure names the URL.

**`deploy/README.md`**, lines 8 and 14: where they list what the venue folder holds, add

`git grep -n "venue.lock" packages/store/src`) and Litestream's `.venue.db-litestream/` directory.

## Appendix: drafting notes

Each drafter recorded, before its tasks, the contract changes, spec problems and open questions it found, with evidence. They are kept here as provenance; where one conflicts with the Reconciliation section above, the Reconciliation wins.

### Notes from draft-task0.md

# Slice 2 plan — Task 0 (image shrink), drafter's part

Task 0 is a new task the owner added on 2026-09-23. It is not in the spec or in `interfaces.md`, so
everything it introduces is listed under "Contract changes" as an addition. It depends on nothing
else in slice 2 and lands before the stream work.

#### Contract changes

All of these are additions, since the contract has no Task 0 section.

- **New in `@waitron/media`, file `packages/media/src/prepare.ts`:**
  - `prepareImage(bytes: Uint8Array, options: { maxUploadBytes: number }): Promise<PreparedImage>`
  - `interface PreparedImage { readonly bytes: Uint8Array; readonly filename: string; readonly [preparedImageBrand]: true }`.
    Only `prepareImage` makes one, so the compiler refuses to store bytes that skipped it.
  - `STORED_LONG_EDGE = 1600`, `STORED_WEBP_QUALITY = 80`, `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000`.
- **`uploadImage` signature changes** (`packages/media/src/images.ts:203-225`, read). The old one is
  `uploadImage(tx, input: ImageMetadataInput & { bytes: Uint8Array }, options: { fallbackLanguage?; maxUploadBytes })`.
  The new one is `uploadImage(tx, input: ImageMetadataInput & { image: PreparedImage }, options?: { fallbackLanguage?: string })`.
  The size check moves into `prepareImage`, which runs OUTSIDE the transaction.
- **Two new error codes in media's registry** (`packages/media/src/errors.ts`). The registry's
  siblings are `image.invalid_metadata` and `image.invalid_query` (the adjective comes first) and
  `image.too_large` (a `too_*` form):
  - `image.invalid_file: Record<string, never>`: the bytes start like a JPEG, PNG or WebP but sharp
    cannot decode them. HTTP 422.
  - `image.too_many_pixels: { maxPixels: number }`: the header declares more than `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS`.
    HTTP 413.
- **New test helper export** `@waitron/media/testing/sample-image.js`, pointing at
  `packages/media/src/testing/sample-image.ts`:
  `sampleImage(options: { width: number; height: number; format: "jpeg" | "png" | "webp" }): Promise<Uint8Array>`.
- **For Task 4 (measurement 4, restore time "product images included"):** after Task 0 a
  realistic stored photo averages **170.7 KiB**, not the 2.6–5.0 MB of an unshrunk phone photo
  (measured, see "Why these numbers" below). The realistic database Task 4 builds should hold
  photos of that size, or should upload them through `prepareImage`.

#### Spec problems

- **The task brief's premise, not the spec's: "coverage bar 98/98/98/95 for the package".**
  `packages/media` is NOT on the high bar. Its `vitest.config.ts` has
  `thresholds: { statements: 90, lines: 90, functions: 85, branches: 85 }`, and `@waitron/media` is
  not in `HIGH_BAR_PACKAGES` (`scripts/coverage-thresholds.test.ts:41-73`, read). Promoting it is
  already queued as lane C item **C1.19** (`~/waitron-campaign-c/queue.md:139-141`: status
  `pending`, measured there at 93.4 / 95.9 / 93.43 / 87.2, branches 7.80 short, branch
  `test/coverage-media`). If Task 0 also raised the thresholds, it would collide with that branch
  and would need the rest of the package's missing branches written first. **Task 0 leaves the
  thresholds alone and brings every file it adds (`prepare.ts`, `testing/sample-image.ts`) to full
  line and branch coverage.** The owner or the plan assembler should confirm this, or else move
  C1.19 ahead of Task 0.
- None in the spec itself. Its §8.1 measurement 4 ("a database of realistic size, product images
  included") is still right. Only the realistic size changes, and Task 0 adds a dated pointer there.

#### Open questions

1. **Should the 5 MiB input limit be raised now that nothing is stored at full size?** The plan
   keeps it: `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024` (`apps/server/src/boot.ts:296`) and the route's
   fallback (`packages/media/src/routes.ts:63`) are unchanged, and it becomes a limit on what may be
   uploaded rather than on what is stored. I have not measured what current phones produce, so I
   cannot say how many real photos it refuses. Decoding memory is not what constrains it:
   decoding a 49-megapixel JPEG raised memory by 7 MiB, and a 100-megapixel PNG by 29 MiB (measured,
   below).
2. **libvips's licence in the box image.** The prebuilt `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64@1.3.3` is
   `LGPL-3.0-or-later` (npm registry metadata). The sharp binding, `@img/sharp-linux-x64`, is
   `Apache-2.0`. libvips ships as its own shared library file (`libvips-cpp.so.8.18.6`), loaded at
   run time. The image already carries LGPL code: `node:26-slim`'s `/usr/share/doc/libc6/copyright`
   reads `License: LGPL-2.1+`. Whether an LGPL-3 library is acceptable beside the Elastic-2.0
   product is a legal-track decision (`docs/compliance/action-plan.md`), not something I can settle.

#### Findings the task rests on (with evidence)

#### How images flow today

- **Upload.** The dashboard's image library (`packages/media/src/dashboard/image-library.ts`, the
  `#save` method at lines ~256-290, read) posts the chosen `File` unchanged as multipart form data
  (`ImageApi.uploadImage`, `packages/media/src/dashboard/client.ts:62-72`). Nothing on the client
  resizes it: a grep for `canvas|createImageBitmap|OffscreenCanvas|toBlob` over `apps` and
  `packages` source finds no image code. The route `POST /management-api/images`
  (`packages/media/src/routes.ts:107-142`) applies `bodyLimit(maxUploadBytes + 64 KiB)`, then,
  inside ONE `withTransaction` (which takes the venue's single write lock), it authorises, parses the
  body and calls `uploadImage`.
- **Store.** `uploadImage` (`images.ts:203-225`) checks the byte length against `maxUploadBytes`
  (`image.too_large`). It then sniffs magic bytes with `validateImageBytes`
  (`packages/catalogue/src/media.ts:48`, which throws `media.unsupported_type`), builds
  `filename = sha256(bytes) + "." + sniffed extension`, and dedupes on `filename`. It inserts the
  metadata row into `media_images` and **the uploaded bytes, as they came,** into
  `media_image_data.bytes`.
- **The content-addressed name is the hash of the STORED bytes**, which today are the uploaded
  bytes. `MEDIA_FILENAME = /^[0-9a-f]{64}\.(jpg|png|webp)$/` (`routes.ts:43`) and the check
  constraint `media_images_filename_ck` (`src/schema/images.ts`) accept those three extensions.
- **Serve.** `GET /media/:filename` (`routes.ts:160-174`) needs **no session**. It serves the stored
  bytes with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and takes the content type from the
  extension (`readImageBytes`, `images.ts:227-243`).
- **Today's path strips no metadata.** The bytes are stored and served exactly as uploaded, so a
  phone photo's EXIF, including a GPS position if it has one, is served to anyone who has the URL.
  Evidence: the insert at `images.ts:223` writes `input.bytes`, and nothing between the route and
  that line rewrites them.
- **Configuration transfer** (`packages/media/src/configuration-transfer.ts`) copies rows unchanged.
  It validates each row's bytes as at most `MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024`, as a sniffable image type,
  and as `filename === sha256(bytes).ext`, the same rule `uploadImage` uses.
- **What displays images, and at what size.** Only the dashboard does:
  - the library grid, `minmax(190px, 1fr)` columns with images at `width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4/3`
    (`image-library.ts:63-78`);
  - the editor preview, `max-width: 320px` (`image-library.ts:98-107`);
  - the product list's thumbnail (`apps/dashboard/src/widgets/product-list.ts:153`, `::part(thumbnail)`);
  - the categories thumbnail, `var(--wt-tap-min)` square (`apps/dashboard/src/screens/categories-screen.ts:80-88`);
  - the product form's preview (`apps/dashboard/src/widgets/image-upload.ts:80`).

  **The till renders no product images**: there is no `<img` under `apps/till/src`, and
  `apps/till/vite.config.ts:51-53` says "Till-side image rendering is a later slice". **No
  `srcset`, `sizes` or size variant exists anywhere** (grep for `srcset|sizes=` over source: none).
  Every surface asks for the one URL, `/media/<sha256>.<ext>`. Printing does not use product images
  (`packages/printing/src` has no `products.image` or media reference).
- **Seed data.** The demo seed (`apps/server/scripts/demo-seed/seed-media.ts`) calls `uploadImage`
  with the committed tiles under `apps/server/scripts/demo-seed/media/`. These are 256×256 RGB PNGs
  of 1.1–2.6 KB, plus `negroni.png` at 110 KB. The box image copies them to `/app/demo-media`
  (`deploy/Dockerfile`).

#### Choosing the library: sharp

The candidates were checked against each package's own documentation, fetched with `curl` from the
source repositories on 2026-09-23.

- **sharp 0.35.4** (native libvips 8.18.6). `docs/src/content/docs/install.md` on `lovell/sharp` main
  says: prebuilt binaries for "Linux x64 (glibc >= 2.28, musl >= 1.2.5, CPU with SSE4.2)" and "Linux
  ARM64 (glibc >= 2.28, …)"; "Ready-compiled sharp and libvips binaries are provided". For esbuild:
  "Ensure sharp is excluded from bundling via the external configuration … `esbuild app.js --bundle
  --platform=node --external:sharp`". **No install-time script**: the npm registry metadata for
  sharp@0.35.4, @img/sharp-linux-x64@0.35.4, @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64@1.3.3,
  @img/sharp-darwin-arm64@0.35.4, @img/colour@1.1.0, detect-libc@2.1.2 and semver@7.8.5 lists no
  `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall` or `prepare` script. So pnpm's build-script settings do not
  matter, and this repository has none anyway: there is no `onlyBuiltDependencies` or
  `ignoredBuiltDependencies` in the root `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or an `.npmrc`.
  **node:26-slim** is Debian 13.7 with `ldd (Debian GLIBC 2.41-12+deb13u4) 2.41` (measured with
  `docker run --platform linux/amd64 node:26-slim`), which satisfies the 2.28 minimum.
- **jSquash (`@jsquash/jpeg` 1.6.0, `@jsquash/webp` 1.5.0, `@jsquash/resize` 2.1.1, WebAssembly).**
  Its own root README says: "⚠️ There is limited support for Node.js environments … For much better
  Node based alternatives please check out … Sharp."
- **wasm-vips 0.0.18.** Its README says: "This library is still under early development." The
  unpacked package is 12.5 MB, and it needs `SharedArrayBuffer` workers.
- **sharp's own WebAssembly build (`@img/sharp-wasm32`)** is "supported by … runtime environments
  that provide multi-threaded Wasm via Workers". It still has to be left out of the bundle, so it
  saves nothing over the native build.

**Measured, sharp against jSquash** (`measure-jsquash.mjs` and `measure-stall.mjs` in
`scratchpad/task0/`; Apple M5 Pro, darwin/arm64, Node v26.7.0; each resizes to a 1600 long edge and
encodes WebP at quality 80; ten photos):

| | mean | max | longest gap between 5 ms timer ticks during one shrink | memory growth over the run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sharp | 134 ms | 205 ms | **6 ms** | 88 MiB |
| jSquash | 518 ms | 738 ms | **1289 ms** (the whole shrink) | 1027 MiB |

The control for the stall column was a 300 ms busy loop, which the same probe reported as a 300 ms
gap. jSquash runs on the main thread, so a till request arriving during an upload would wait for the
whole shrink. sharp does its work on libvips's own threads.

**The choice is sharp.** It is the fastest option, it leaves the event loop free, its memory use is
small and does not grow, and it has prebuilt glibc binaries for the box's platform. Its costs are
that it must stay out of the esbuild bundle (`--external:sharp`) and that the image must carry a
`node_modules/` beside the bundle, which the next section shows working.

**The packaging, measured end to end** (`scratchpad/task0/image-probe/probe.sh`). This was a stand-in
for the Dockerfile. Its build stage was `node:26` on `linux/amd64` running `pnpm@9.15.0`,
`pnpm add sharp@0.35.4 esbuild@0.28.2`, an esbuild bundle built with the server's own flags plus
`--external:sharp`, and then `cp -rL node_modules/.pnpm/sharp@0.35.4/node_modules/. <app>/node_modules/`.
Its runtime was `node:26-slim` on `linux/amd64`. The results:

- The bundle printed `bundle ran sharp 0.35.4 on linux/x64: webp 1600x1067`.
- Control: the same bundle with no `node_modules` beside it failed with
  `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'sharp' imported from /app/server.js`.
- pnpm 9 installs BOTH the glibc and the musl builds (`@img+sharp-linuxmusl-x64@0.35.4` was
  present). The flattened directory is 38 MB. With `@img/*linuxmusl*` removed it is 20 MB, and the
  bundle still ran.
- **esbuild does not refuse to bundle sharp.** With the repository's esbuild 0.28.2 and no
  `--external`, the build exits 0. Running it then fails with
  `Dynamic require of "…" is not supported`. The external form keeps one literal `import("sharp")`
  in the output and the bundled form keeps none (grep counts 1 and 0), which is what the CI check in
  Step 13 relies on.
- `node --input-type=module -e "await import('sharp')"` run with working directory `/app` resolves
  `/app/node_modules/sharp` (measured in the same container). The image-smoke step relies on this.

**Why sharp is loaded lazily.** `packages/provisioning` bundles `@waitron/composition`, which
imports `@waitron/media` (`packages/provisioning/src/bin.ts:7`, `packages/composition/src/modules.ts:1`).
Nothing places sharp beside that bundle, and in pnpm's layout sharp cannot be found from
`packages/provisioning/dist`. So a top-level `import sharp` would stop `waitron-provision` from
starting at all. With `import("sharp")` inside `prepareImage`, only an upload needs sharp.

#### Why these numbers: a 1600-pixel long edge, WebP at quality 80

**Measured** (`measure-sharp.mjs`; the same machine; `out-sharp-darwin.txt`). Ten Wikimedia Commons
food and bar photos were used: `in/photo1.jpg` to `in/photo10.jpg`, 2.58–4.97 MB each, 3072–5312 px
on the long side, 36.9 MB together.

| setting | mean stored | ×5,000 | mean time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WebP q80, 1600 | 170.7 KiB | **0.87 GB** | 131 ms |
| WebP q75, 1600 | 136.9 KiB | 0.70 GB | 127 ms |
| WebP q80, 1200 | 110.5 KiB | 0.57 GB | 83 ms |
| WebP q80, 2048 | 250.7 KiB | 1.28 GB | 187 ms |
| JPEG q80 (mozjpeg), 1600 | 202.5 KiB | 1.04 GB | 119 ms |

With one libvips thread (`sharp.concurrency(1)`), WebP q80 at 1600 took a mean of 138 ms and a
maximum of 211 ms. The box's N100-class processor is **unmeasured**. The same ten photos stored as
they came average 3.69 MB, which is 18.4 GB for 5,000, inside the owner's 10–24 GB estimate.

- **1600 px on the long side.** The largest place a photo is drawn today is 320 CSS px wide (the
  editor preview). A photo 800 CSS px wide on a screen with two device pixels per CSS pixel needs
  1600 px. That covers a product photo filling half a landscape tablet, or a wide online-menu card.
  Those surfaces are planned; this is reasoning, not a measurement. 1600 meets the "about 1 GB for
  5,000" target (0.87 GB) where 2048 does not (1.28 GB), and 1200 would halve today's largest
  high-density display headroom for 0.30 GB saved.
- **WebP, always.** It keeps transparency: a 2400×1200 half-transparent PNG came out `hasAlpha=true`
  (`probe-shrink.mjs`). It is 16% smaller than mozjpeg JPEG at the same quality number (the table
  above). One output format also means one content type for every new upload. The only consumers are
  browsers. The dashboard and the till are web pages, and printing does not read product images.
- **The aspect ratio is kept and nothing is enlarged.** Using `fit: "inside"` with
  `withoutEnlargement: true`, a 300×225 photo stays 300×225, and without `withoutEnlargement` it
  becomes 1600×1200 (`probe-controls.mjs`).
- **Upright, then every tag gone.** `autoOrient: true` applies the EXIF orientation and removes the
  tag. sharp's output documentation: "By default all metadata will be removed, which includes
  EXIF-based orientation"; `keepMetadata`: "The default behaviour … is to … strip all metadata,
  including the removal of any ICC profile." Measured (`probe-rotate.mjs`, `probe-controls.mjs`): a
  3072×2304 JPEG tagged orientation 6 with a GPS block came out 1200×1600 with no EXIF and no XMP.
  Without `autoOrient` it came out 1600×1200, which is sideways. Adding `.keepExif()` kept the GPS
  block.
- **Inputs:** JPEG, PNG and WebP, as today; `validateImageBytes` still gates the type. **Output:**
  WebP. An animated WebP yields its first frame (sharp's `pages` option defaults to `1`, per the
  constructor documentation; I have not measured this).
- **Refusals.**
  - Header-only garbage makes `metadata()` throw `Input buffer has corrupt header`.
  - A JPEG cut in half passes `metadata()`, and the pipeline then throws `premature end of JPEG image`.
  - A 10001×10000 PNG is only 311 KB, but it declares 100,010,000 pixels. Reading its header takes
    0.3 ms.

  All ten real photos pass under sharp's default `failOn: "warning"`, which is the setting its
  documentation recommends "with untrusted input" (`probe-failon.mjs`).
- **The same upload always gives the same bytes.** Each of the ten photos shrank to byte-identical
  output on two runs, and the hashes on darwin/arm64 matched the hashes on linux/amd64 in
  `node:26-slim` (`out-probe-darwin.txt`, `out-probe-linux-amd64.txt`). So "uploading the same file
  again finds the existing image" (`docs/content-and-images.md`) still holds. It holds only while the
  sharp and libvips versions and the settings stay the same, because the name is the hash of the
  STORED bytes.
- **Memory is small even for huge inputs** (`probe-pixels.mjs`, with the operation cache off).
  Memory rose by 7 MiB for a 49 MP JPEG, 15 MiB for a 49 MP PNG and 29 MiB for a 100 MP PNG. So
  `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000` is a cap on work, not on memory.

#### What happens to the name, the limits, and photos already stored

- **The name stays the hash of the stored bytes.** The alternative, hashing the original, would
  break the one invariant the public URL rests on: an `immutable` URL names exactly the bytes it
  serves. It would also break configuration transfer's check (`configuration-transfer.ts:60`), which
  recomputes the name from the stored bytes.

  What changes: a new upload's name is the hash of the shrunk WebP, with extension `.webp`. The same
  original uploaded after a sharp or libvips upgrade, or after a settings change, may shrink to
  different bytes and create a second library entry instead of reusing the first. That is accepted:
  it costs one duplicate photo the operator can delete.

  Existing rows keep their names and bytes. `MEDIA_FILENAME` and `media_images_filename_ck` keep
  accepting `.jpg` and `.png`, because rows with those names still arrive through configuration
  transfer and are still in dev venues. So `readImageBytes` keeps all three content types.
- **The 5 MiB cap stays as the limit on what may be uploaded** (open question 1). The route's
  `bodyLimit` is unchanged.
- **`configuration-transfer.ts`'s `MAX_BYTES` stays at 5 MiB, and imports are not shrunk.** A
  bundle's product rows name its photos by filename, and the import copies rows unchanged ("preserving
  immutable URL contents on import", `configuration-transfer.ts:34`). Shrinking there would change
  names that other rows in the same bundle point at. A bundle exported after Task 0 already holds
  shrunk photos.
- **Photos already stored:** CLAUDE.md §3 says "No backwards-compatibility or data-migration code
  until Waitron is in production." No venue is live. A dev venue seeded before Task 0 keeps its
  full-size PNG tiles, which remain valid rows. `wa-wt reset demo <name>` rebuilds it, and the
  re-seed runs every tile through `prepareImage` (Step 11), so they come back as WebP.

#### Realistic size of 5,000 photos after shrinking

**About 0.87 GB (0.81 GiB).** This is **estimated from a measurement**: a mean of 170.7 KiB per
photo over ten real 2.6–5.0 MB food and bar photos, multiplied by 5,000. The per-photo range was
59–338 KB. If all 5,000 were like the largest of the ten, the total would be about 1.7 GB.

### Notes from draft-task1.md

# Slice 2 plan — Task 1 (drafted as Task 1a and Task 1b)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-sqlite-slice2-stream-and-cold-restore-design.md` §2.

**Why two pull requests.** Task 1 touches two unrelated mechanisms. 1a keys the machine's own rows by
node id: `packages/db`, the deployment/mirror/join code in `apps/server`, four root guards and the
prose that said `local` tables would move into `node.db` — about 40 files, most of them tests whose
call sites gain a node id argument. 1b hashes session cookies: `packages/identity`, the till and
dashboard cookie paths in `apps/server`, and every test that builds a cookie from a session — about 60
files, most of them one-token test edits. A reviewer can accept or reject each on its own. **1b must
land after 1a**: 1b's migration recreates two tables, and the scanner that lets the classification
guards follow a recreated table is added in 1a (1a, Step 1).

#### Contract changes

1. **`deployment` is split rather than given a `node_id`.** `deployment` keeps the environment stamp
   (one row, `id = 1`) and is reclassified `state`; a NEW `local` table **`node_roles`** (`node_id`
   primary key) takes `mode`, `singleton_role` and `break_glass_verifier`. Why: the environment belongs
   to the database, not the machine — CLAUDE.md §5, "One database per environment". Keyed by node, a
   node with no row of its own would read "not stamped" from a stamped database and could stamp it
   again for a different environment. Keeping `deployment` also leaves `deploy/waitron.sh:198`
   (`select environment from deployment where id = 1`) and `waitron-provision`'s stamping untouched.
   The dead `fence_lsn` column is dropped rather than moved: `packages/db/src/schema/deployment.ts:44`
   records that nothing reads it.
2. **Every per-node reader and writer gains a `nodeId: string` argument**, placed straight after the
   handle: `readDeploymentMode`, `readSingletonRole`, `readDeploymentAxes`, `setDeploymentMode(Tx)`,
   `setSingletonRole(Tx)`, `readBreakGlassVerifier`, `setBreakGlassVerifierTx`, `readMirrorConfig`,
   `writeMirrorConfig` (all `packages/db`); `refreshDeploymentHolders`, `mintBreakGlassSecret`,
   `verifyBreakGlass`, `commitMirrorPromotionTx`, and `PromoteApiDeps.nodeId` (all `apps/server`).
   `stampDeployment`, `readDeploymentEnvironment` and `deploymentTableExists` are unchanged.
   `join_requests` gains `node_id`, but no signature changes: every verb in
   `apps/server/src/join-requests.ts` already takes `cfg: TillConfig`, which carries `nodeId`.
3. **`hashSessionToken(raw: string): string`** as the contract states. A sibling,
   `mintSessionToken(): string`, stays inside `@waitron/identity` and is not exported. Tokens are
   `randomUUID()` values — the same generator `newId` uses (`packages/db/src/schema/columns.ts:270`),
   so the cookie carries exactly as much randomness as it did as a row id. They also keep the UUID
   shape that the `isUuid` screens in `apps/server/src/till-session.ts` and
   `packages/server-kit/src/management-cookie.ts` check.
4. **`ManagementSession` becomes `{ token: string; personId: string }`** — the `id` field is removed,
   so the compiler finds every place that put a row id into a cookie. The till's **`Session` gains
   `token`** and keeps `id`, because `authorize` (`packages/identity/src/authorize.ts:50-54`) looks a
   till session up by row id. `requireSession` (`apps/server/src/till-session.ts`) now returns that
   row id as `sessionId`; before, it returned the cookie value. `resolveManagementSession`,
   `endManagementSession` and `endSession` take the RAW token and hash it themselves. The parameter
   names `managementSessionId` (profile, layouts, bookings, media, venue-service, `authorizeManager`)
   and `sessionId` stay as they are, carrying the token: renaming them would touch about 150 call
   sites with no change in behaviour.
5. **Seven `local` tables are reclassified `state` instead of gaining `node_id`**: `deployment` (item
   1), `node_membership` (spec §2 already settles it as one row), `scheduled_runs`, `sessions`,
   `management_sessions`, `webauthn_challenges`, `totp_enrollments` and `google_oidc_states`. The
   reasoning for each is in 1a's and 1b's tables below. `tenant_credentials` and `change_log` stay
   `local` without a `node_id` (see Spec problems).
6. **`tablesCreatedBy` (`packages/sync-enrolment/src/migration-tables.ts`) follows
   `ALTER TABLE … RENAME TO …`.** drizzle-kit rebuilds a SQLite table whose primary key, check
   constraints or not-null flags change, by creating `__new_<table>`, copying, dropping and renaming.
   The scanner today counts only CREATE and DROP, so after such a migration both classification guards
   would report `__new_<table>` as unclassified and `<table>` as having no creator. No migration in
   the tree has rebuilt a table yet: `grep -rln "__new_\|RENAME TO" packages/*/drizzle/*.sql` prints
   nothing.
7. **`scripts/write-path-tables.test.ts` covers `node_roles`**, which inherits `deployment`'s rule
   (application code may read it and never write it). Its cross-check against the frozen privilege
   matrix gains a named list of tables created after the matrix froze. That list has one entry.

#### Spec problems

1. **Spec §2 defines `local` as "belongs to one node, keyed by its id". Two tables the spec itself
   keeps cannot meet that definition.** `change_log` "needs nothing" (§2). `tenant_credentials` is
   tied to its node by a seal, not a column: a row sealed under one box's key ring fails with
   `credentials.decrypt_failed` on any other box (`packages/credentials/src/store.ts`,
   `tryGetCredential`). §3.3 already decides that slice 3's first task moves the vault to a venue key,
   which turns these rows into venue rows. Adding `node_id` now would change about 27 files (every
   caller of the credentials store) only for slice 3 to undo it. So the plan words the class as
   "belongs to one node; the table's reason says what ties a row to its node": a `node_id` column
   (`node_roles`, `mirror_config`, `join_requests`), a seal (`tenant_credentials`), or never
   outliving the transaction that wrote it (`change_log`). The owner can overrule this for
   `tenant_credentials` (Open question 2).
2. **§2 says of leftover `change_log` rows that "nothing reads them from a restored copy". That is not
   what the code does.** `drainChangeLog` (`packages/db/src/change-log.ts:47-54`) runs
   `delete from change_log returning payload` inside every `withTransaction`. So a rebuilt box's
   first write transaction removes the leftover rows and hands them to the dashboard's listeners, and
   each tells the dashboard that a resource changed and should be read again. That is read from the
   code, not run. It is harmless — each row only names which resource changed, and re-reading it is
   what a dashboard does anyway — but the reason string below says what happens, not what §2 says.
3. **§2 lists `deployment` among the tables to key by node id.** Keying it whole breaks the
   one-database-per-environment rule (Contract change 1), so the plan splits the table instead.

#### Open questions

1. **Should a login survive a promotion?** Sessions are not keyed by node (1b), so a till's shift
   and a dashboard sign-in stay valid after a rebuild (same node) and — once slice 3 exists — after
   another node is promoted over the same data. The alternative is to key them by node, which would
   log every till and dashboard out at promotion. Slice 2 behaves the same either way, because a
   rebuild keeps the node id. The plan's default is not to key them. This is a product decision for
   slice 3, not something the code settles.
2. **`tenant_credentials` without `node_id`** (Spec problem 1). The default is to leave it unkeyed
   until slice 3 replaces the per-node seal. Say if you want it keyed now anyway.

### Notes from draft-task2-3.md

# Draft: Tasks 2 and 3

Tasks 2 and 3 are each split in two, one pull request per part, because each contract task holds
two changes a reviewer could accept or reject separately (see "Contract changes", item 1). Order:
2a → 2b, and 3a → 3b. 2b needs 2a. 3b needs 3a. Neither pair depends on the other, but 2b's
migration and Task 1's migration are both in the core set, so whichever lands second regenerates
(CLAUDE.md §3, the collision rule).

#### Contract changes

1. **Task 2 is 2a + 2b, and Task 3 is 3a + 3b**, one branch and one pull request each. 2a is the
   recovery key without an archive destination; 2b is the locked state row. 3a is the lock on the
   venue folder; 3b is the restart reset.
2. **`apps/server/src/recovery-state.ts` already exists.** It holds the boot escalation counter
   (`readRecoveryState`, `writeRecoveryState`, `recovery.json`), and `recovery-surface.ts` imports it.
   A second meaning of "recovery state" beside it would be a trap, so the new module is
   **`apps/server/src/sealed-state.ts`**, the table is **`node_sealed_state`** (Drizzle export
   `nodeSealedState`), and the names become:
   - `collectRecoveryEntries` → `collectSealedEntries(deps: { stateDir: string; modules: readonly WaitronModule[]; resolvers: Record<string, string>; manifest: BackupManifest }): Promise<ArchiveEntry[]>`
     (it also needs `modules` and `resolvers`, because the module non-database state is collected
     from them — `collectModuleNonDbState(modules, resolvers)` in `backup-sources.ts`);
   - `sealRecoveryState` → `sealNodeState(entries: ArchiveEntry[], recoveryKey: string): Promise<Uint8Array>`
     and `unsealRecoveryState` → `unsealNodeState(sealed: Uint8Array, recoveryKey: string): ArchiveEntry[]`.
     `unsealNodeState` is **synchronous** (`decryptArtifact` and `unpackArchive` are). `sealNodeState`
     returns a promise (changed 2026-09-24, on Task 2b's branch): it derives the key with
     `encryptArtifactAsync`, off the event loop, so a refresh does not stall sales;
   - `writeRecoveryStateRow` → `writeSealedStateRow(tx: Transaction, nodeId: string, sealed: Uint8Array, at: Date): Promise<void>`;
   - `readRecoveryStateRow` → `readSealedStateRow(tx: Transaction, nodeId: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null>`;
   - `refreshRecoveryState(deps)` → `createSealedStateRefresher(deps: SealedStateDeps): SealedStateRefresher`,
     whose `refresh(): Promise<SealedStateOutcome>` (`"sealed" | "no_key" | "failed"`) never
     throws and runs one refresh at a time (see Task 2b for why both matter).
3. **The `sealed` column is `binary`, not base64 text.** `packages/db/src/schema/columns.ts`
   already has `binary(name)`, which stores a `blob` and hands back a `Uint8Array`; it is used by
   `print_jobs.payload`, `tenant_credentials.ciphertext` and `media_image_data.bytes`. No vocabulary
   change, so `scripts/column-vocabulary.test.ts` is untouched.
4. **`loadRecoveryKey(env)` as contracted**, plus `writeRecoveryKey(stateDir, { recoveryKey, keyRotatedAt })`
   in `backup-env-writer.ts` (writes the key into `backup.env` keeping every other line), and two
   new `BackupApiDeps` fields: `readRecoveryKey: () => Promise<string | undefined>` (2a) and
   `sealedState: SealedStateRefresher` (2b).
5. **The lock's error code is `provisioning.database_in_use` with `{ database: string }`, not
   `store.venue_in_use` with `{ directory }`.** A code names the domain concept, never the throwing
   package (CLAUDE.md §3); its siblings are `provisioning.database_unreachable`,
   `provisioning.database_ahead`, `provisioning.database_unmigrated` and
   `provisioning.database_not_owned`, which all name the venue DIRECTORY as `database`. It is
   declared in `packages/db/src/errors.ts`, not in `packages/store`: `packages/store` imports nothing
   from the workspace (its `package.json` has only `drizzle-orm`; `index.ts` says why), so it throws
   a plain `VenueInUseError` class and `@waitron/db` turns it into the `AppError`.
6. **The lock is shared inside one process.** `packages/store` gains
   `lockVenueDirectory(directory: string): Promise<VenueLock>` (`VenueLock = { release(): void }`),
   counted per process: the server opens the same folder more than once at the same time
   (`BackupSupervisor` opens its own handle — `backup-supervisor.ts`, `reload()` — beside boot's),
   so a lock that refused a second opener in the same process would refuse the backup. Only a
   second PROCESS is refused. `openVenueStore` gains `exclusive?: boolean` (default true);
   `@waitron/db` gains `openVenueDatabase(directory, { exclusive? })` and
   `lockVenueDatabase(directory): Promise<VenueLock>`.
7. **The reset is reached through a new fiscal-slot seat**,
   `FiscalContribution.resetInFlight(deps: { db: Database }, now: Date): Promise<number>`
   (`packages/fiscal/src/contribution.ts`), because `boot.ts` names no regime package
   (`scripts/module-seams.test.ts`) and reaches the drain the same way (`enabledFiscal.drain`).
   `resetInFlightClaims(tx, now)` in `drain.ts` is as contracted; the Veri*Factu seat calls it.

#### Spec problems

1. **§6: "a second opener is refused" would break two documented operator procedures.**
   `deploy/README.md` (the "operator CLIs" section) tells an operator to run break-glass with
   `docker compose exec` — "A command that needs the server RUNNING" — and `apps/server/README.md`
   says of `waitron-credentials set --purpose email.smtp`: "rotating it does not require a restart".
   Two development scripts, `record-one-sale.ts` and `settle-invoice-first.ts`, also write sales for
   the running server's drain to send (their headers say so). None of these files anything, which is
   the property the reset needs. The plan keeps the lock ON by default and gives exactly these four
   an explicit `exclusive: false`, which takes no lock at all. Everything else — a second server,
   the cold restore, rejoin, `waitron-provision venue`, `register-till` — is refused while a server
   runs. Open question 1 asks the owner whether to keep that exception.
2. **§3.1: "rewrites the row whenever one of those files changes" is met by "at every start, and
   after every write this process makes", not by watching files.** Read, not run: in trading mode
   the only writers of the eight files inside the running server are the backup routes
   (`backup-api.ts`, `apply` and `rotate`, through `writeBackupEnv`). Every other writer is followed
   by a restart before trading continues: `ensureBoxSecrets` and provisioning/adoption
   (`writeTradingEnv`, `writeModuleConfig`) run in setup mode, which ends in a restart; mirror
   promotion writes `trading.env` and then sends itself `SIGTERM` (`boot.ts`, `promoteMirrorRun`);
   `clearTradingEnv` runs in the stopped-server `waitron-rejoin`. A file an operator edits by hand is
   sealed at the next start. Task 9's certificate re-issue on first start after a rebuild must run
   BEFORE boot's refresh call, or the row carries the dead box's certificate until the next start.
3. **§3.1's row has no subject in setup mode.** A box in setup mode has no node id
   (`config.till` is unset), so no row is written until the first trading start. That start follows
   provisioning at once, so the gap is one restart; stated so nobody assumes otherwise.

#### Open questions

1. **Should break-glass and `waitron-credentials` keep running beside a live server?** The plan
   says yes (spec problem 1), because both are documented that way and neither files anything. The
   stricter alternative — every tool refused while the server runs — would change both documented
   procedures to "stop the box first", and a certificate or SMTP rotation would then need downtime.
   This is a product decision about operator procedure, not a code question.
