### Notes from draft-task4-5.md

# Slice 2 plan — draft for Tasks 4 and 5

Drafted 2026-09-23 against `main` at `cb809f1b5`. Everything cited below was read on that tree; the
three claims about the S3 client's behaviour were RUN, in a scratch script outside the repository
(`node` v26.7.0 against `@aws-sdk/client-s3` 3.1136.0 resolved from `bench/sqlite-failover`, with a
scripted request handler in place of the network), and the Litestream settings were read from
<https://litestream.io/reference/config/> and <https://litestream.io/reference/restore/>, fetched with
`curl` on 2026-09-23.

#### Contract changes

1. **`stream.precondition_failed` becomes `backup.stream_precondition_failed`.** Error codes name the
   domain concept and follow their siblings' prefix (CLAUDE.md §3). Every backup-related code today
   is `backup.*` — `apps/server/src/errors.ts:1524-1642` (`backup.artifact_invalid`,
   `backup.recovery_key_missing`, `backup.destination_failed`, …) — and the contract's own alert
   proposals are `backup.stream_*`. A new `stream.` prefix would sit beside them the way the
   `payments.`/`payment.` mistake CLAUDE.md §1 records did. Three more codes the package needs are
   added in the same family: `backup.stream_request_failed` (any other bucket failure),
   `backup.stream_pointer_invalid` (a `current.json` this package did not write) and
   `backup.stream_name_invalid` (a venue id, node id, term or time that cannot form a key).
2. **`createS3ObjectStore(config, options?)`** — an optional second argument
   `S3ObjectStoreOptions = { requestHandler?: S3ClientConfig["requestHandler"]; sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void> }`.
   Additive. It is how the unit tests put a scripted network under the real client, and how they
   keep the conflict back-off out of wall-clock time.
3. **`probeBucket(store, nonce?)` returns `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: ProbeFailure; detail: string }`**,
   where `ProbeFailure` is a fixed union (`"unreachable" | "access_denied" |
   "conditional_write_unsupported" | "write_failed" | "read_mismatch" | "list_failed" |
   "create_only_ignored" | "fresh_version_refused" | "if_match_ignored" | "delete_failed"`) instead of
   a free `reason: string`. Task 8's screen can then put translated copy on each reason; `detail` is
   the store's own answer for the log.
4. **New exports Task 6, 9 and 10 will want**, all additive: `signPointer(body, privateKeyPkcs8)`,
   `pointerMessage(body)`, `pointerKey(venueId)`, `markerKey(venueId, generation)`,
   `generationPrefix(venueId, generation)`, `parseGenerationName(name)`, `GENERATION_NAME`,
   `bucketKey(config, key)`, `normalisePrefix(prefix)`, `CONFLICT_ATTEMPTS`, `PRUNE_CONCURRENCY`,
   `PROBE_PREFIX`, and a test-support entry point `@waitron/stream/testing/memory-store.js`
   (`createMemoryObjectStore`) — the in-memory store with real conditional-write rules, which Task 6's
   supervisor tests can reuse instead of writing a second fake.
5. **Suggestion for Task 6's drafter (not changed here):** `SupervisorDeps.sign(bytes: Uint8Array)`
   does not fit what `@waitron/membership` offers. `signBytes(message: string, privateKeyB64: string)`
   (`packages/membership/src/crypto.ts:16`) signs a UTF-8 STRING. Task 5 exports
   `pointerMessage(body): string`, so `sign(message: string): Promise<string>` would let
   `apps/server` implement it as `signBytes(message, key)` with no decode step.
6. **Keys the `ObjectStore` sees are relative to `BucketConfig.prefix`.** `createS3ObjectStore`
   prepends the normalised prefix on the way out and strips it from `list` results on the way in, so
   `venuePrefix(venueId)` (`venues/<id>/`) is the same string whatever prefix the owner chose. Task 6
   writes Litestream's replica path with `bucketKey(config, generationPrefix(venueId, generation))`
   so the two cannot disagree.
7. **Task 4 produces one more value than the contract lists:** `LINUX_BINARIES_RUN` plus the
   SHA-256 of both Linux release archives, which Task 6's image step pins. And measurement 2 gains an
   arm "2b" (below, under Spec problems, item 6).

#### Spec problems

1. **§4.4 says the pointer is signed "with the node's membership key (`packages/membership`,
   `signDocumentBody`)".** `signDocumentBody` is typed `(body: MembershipDocumentBody, …)`
   (`packages/membership/src/verify.ts:36`); it cannot sign a pointer. The plan signs with the same
   key through `signBytes` over `canonicalize(...)` — the two primitives `signDocumentBody` is built
   from — and puts a purpose tag inside the signed bytes (`{ purpose: "waitron.stream.pointer.v1",
   pointer: … }`) so a signature over a pointer can never be presented as a signature over some other
   document the same key signs. Same key, same algorithm, different entry point.
2. **"A refused pointer write means another box is writing this venue" (§4.4) has one exception the
   spec does not cover: our own write, answered twice.** The pinned client retries a server error by
   default. Run 2026-09-23 against `@aws-sdk/client-s3` 3.1136.0 with a scripted handler: a `500`
   then a `200` on a `PutObject` carrying `IfMatch` made **two** calls and succeeded; a `409` made
   one call and threw `ConditionalRequestConflict`; a `412` made one call and threw
   `PreconditionFailed`. So a conditional write whose first attempt LANDED and lost its answer is
   retried, and the retry is refused with 412 — which the spec's rule reads as another box. The plan
   keeps the rule and narrows it: a 412 is a loss **unless the object now holds exactly the bytes
   this call wrote**. Every conditional write this package makes carries bytes no other writer can
   produce (a pointer is signed by the writing node's own key over its own term and time; a marker
   carries a random nonce), so equal bytes can only be our own write. Stated here because it is a
   behaviour the spec did not write down.
3. **§4.5's "the generation name gains a per-node counter" (the branch taken if a restart does not
   re-upload) looks redundant with §4.4's name.** `gen-<term>-<node-id>-<opened-at, UTC>` already
   differs between two openings more than a second apart, and the create-only marker refuses two
   openings in the same second. Task 5's `generationName` therefore takes no counter on either branch
   of measurement 1. If the owner wants the counter anyway it is one extra argument; Task 6's drafter
   should settle it with the owner rather than silently adding or dropping it.
4. **§8.1 item 3 ("which restore points survive a 168-hour window") cannot be measured literally in a
   task:** it would take a week of wall-clock time. Task 4 measures it on a compressed schedule that
   keeps the ORDER of every interval (30-second, 5-minute and hourly merges, the daily full copy, the
   retention window) but not their ratios, and states the result as "which kind of file survives which
   boundary", not as hours. The extrapolation to 168 hours is labelled as one.
5. **§8.1 item 4 ("a database of realistic size, product images included") has no size to work
   from.** Nothing in the repository records how many product images a venue holds. The upload cap
   is 5 MiB per image (`packages/media/src/routes.ts:63`, `maxUploadBytes ?? 5 * 1024 * 1024`) and
   images are stored whole in `media_image_data.bytes` (`packages/media/src/images.ts`,
   `uploadImage`). Task 4 runs two sizes — an assumed typical one and every image at the cap — and
   labels both `assumed-not-measured`. See Open questions.
6. **§4.5 does not account for a Litestream setting that bounds the side file on its own, by
   blocking.** The configuration reference, fetched with `curl` 2026-09-23, documents
   `truncate-page-n` (since v0.5.3, behaviour revised in v0.5.15, so present on the 0.5.17 pin):
   _"Emergency threshold for the TRUNCATE checkpoint (default: 121359, ~500MB). When the WAL crosses
   this threshold Litestream first attempts a non-blocking PASSIVE checkpoint and only forces a
   blocking TRUNCATE (which blocks both readers and writers) when that passive checkpoint does not
   bring the WAL back below the threshold."_ The prototype's offline run stopped at 308 MB
   (results note, S4), so nothing has seen what this does while the bucket is unreachable.
   **2026-09-23:** arm 2b drove an offline side file past the threshold for a few seconds only; it did
   not shrink, and what the emergency checkpoint does over longer was not established (results note,
   Slice 2 measurements §2). If it
   fires there, it is Litestream putting a blocking checkpoint on the sale path, below whatever limit
   Task 6 picks. Task 4 adds an arm (2b) that drives an offline side file past 500 MB and records the
   longest commit and whether the file shrank. Task 6's side-file limit must be chosen knowing the
   answer, or set `truncate-page-n` explicitly.
7. **§4.2's checksum:** the release API publishes a SHA-256 digest per asset. Read 2026-09-23 with
   `curl -sSL -H "accept: application/vnd.github+json" https://api.github.com/repos/benbjohnson/litestream/releases/tags/v0.5.17`:
   `litestream-0.5.17-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` →
   `sha256:cfb371176d164437ae869f8351cfde49bd1804ae71c61923f75c9cba9c9c006d`;
   `litestream-0.5.17-linux-arm64.tar.gz` →
   `sha256:f8ca4a050095c1efbda2c4365172e61bf9d955ea0d9ac42f448b52e51819baa5`. The release also carries
   `checksums.txt`. Measurement 5 recomputes both digests from the downloaded bytes; Task 6 pins the
   values measurement 5 records, not these.

#### Open questions

1. **How many product photos will the deli have, and roughly how large?** Only used to size
   measurement 4. Without an answer, the run uses 300 images of 400 KiB (assumed) and 300 at the
   5 MiB cap (upper bound), both labelled as assumptions.

### Notes from draft-task6-7.md

# Slice 2 plan — draft for Tasks 6 and 7

Drafted 2026-09-23 against `main` at `cb809f1b5`. Every file, function, line range, command and
external fact below was read (or run, where it says so) while drafting.

#### Contract changes

1. **`SupervisorDeps.sign(message: string): Promise<string>`**, not `sign(bytes: Uint8Array)`. The
   membership key signs a STRING: `signBytes(message: string, privateKeyB64: string)`
   (`packages/membership/src/crypto.ts:16`). So the supervisor needs the exact text the pointer's
   signature covers, and **Task 5 must export `pointerMessage(body: StreamPointer): string`** — the
   same text `verifyPointer` checks — so the signer and the verifier cannot drift.
2. **`SupervisorDeps` gains `log`, `sleep?`, and (Task 7) `onCommit`.** A supervisor that restarts a
   child process has to say why (spec §7: "Litestream's status can go in the logs"), and every
   waiting loop takes an injected sleep, the pattern `BackupSupervisorDeps.sleep` already uses
   (`apps/server/src/backup-supervisor.ts:98`). If Task 4 records `AUTOCHECKPOINT_OFF_NEEDED = true`,
   it also gains `setAutoCheckpoint(on: boolean): Promise<void>`.
3. **`foldBack()` and `checkpointTruncate()` return `Promise<{ reclaimed: boolean }>`**, not `void`.
   The fold-back can be refused by a reader still holding the side file (measured, Task 6 Step 5
   below), and the supervisor has to know to try again.
4. **`StreamStatus`:** `reason` is `string | null` rather than optional; it gains `stateSince: string`
   and `bucketProblem: { reason: string; since: string } | null`, which the alerts need for `since`.
   `lagMs` and `lastConfirmedUploadAt` arrive in **Task 7**, which is where they are computed. Task 7
   also exports `StreamView = StreamStatus | { state: "off" }` from `@waitron/stream`.
5. **The dev/CI setup script is `scripts/setup-litestream.ts`, not `.mjs`.** The root Vitest project
   measures coverage over every `scripts/**/*.mjs` at 98/98/98/95 (`vitest.config.ts:116-117`), and a
   download script has nothing a unit test can assert without the network. A `.ts` under `scripts/`
   is measured by no table (the same file's comment on `scripts/dev-server-proxy.ts`), and Node 26
   runs it directly, as the bench rig runs `node src/setup-litestream.ts`.
   — corrected 2026-09-24: review found the `.ts` script untested and unmeasured, so it became
   `scripts/setup-litestream.mjs` with a root suite, `scripts/setup-litestream.test.mjs`, that injects
   the download and the platform and so needs no network. Later tasks name the `.mjs`.
6. **The credentials purpose `backup.stream` is defined in Task 6, not Task 8**, because Task 6's boot
   wiring has to read it; Task 8 writes it. It carries a **`venueId`** field the contract did not list
   (the kit and every key need one, and nothing else in the tree names a venue id — `grep -rn venueId
   apps/server/src` finds none). The vault refuses empty strings (`validatePayload`,
   `packages/credentials/src/purposes.ts`), so an absent `endpoint` or `prefix` is stored as `-`, the
   convention `payments.sumup`'s affiliate fields already use (same file, its comment).
7. **`computeLag`'s input is settled** as
   `{ pending: readonly (readonly [number, number])[]; newestUploadAt: Date | null; skewMs: number; now: Date }`
   returning `{ lagMs: number; coveredUpTo: number | null }`, beside a `CommitLog` class that produces
   `pending`. Reasons in Task 7.
8. **`onCommit` is on the store's internal `Connections` too** (`packages/store/src/connections.ts`),
   because the three places a commit happens — the write queue, the adapter's direct transaction and
   the adapter's statement runner — all hold a `Connections`, not a `StoreHandle`.
9. **Assumptions about Task 5 this draft relies on**, each one line to adjust if Task 5 differs:
   `ObjectStore` keys are relative to `BucketConfig.prefix` (the store adds it), and `list(prefix)`
   returns keys in that same relative form; `BucketConfig.prefix` is `""` or ends in `/`; the claim
   marker's key is `venuePrefix(venueId) + generation + "/opened.json"`; `stream.precondition_failed`
   is registered in `packages/stream/src/errors.ts`; `probeBucket` answers `{ ok: false }` only when the
   bucket answered with a refusal and THROWS when it got no answer at all; the package's barrel is
   `packages/stream/src/index.ts`.

#### Spec problems

1. **§4.5 "folds the file back from a connection outside the write queue's sale path" cannot be done
   literally without stalling the whole server.** Measured 2026-09-23 on Node v26.7.0, SQLite 3.53.4
   (`scratchpad/probe/ckpt.mjs`, `ckpt2.mjs`, `ckpt3.mjs`):
   - on a THIRD connection while the writer holds an open transaction, `pragma
     wal_checkpoint(truncate)` waited out the whole busy timeout (1594.7 ms at a 1500 ms timeout) and
     returned `busy: 1` with the file unchanged. `node:sqlite` is synchronous, so that wait blocks the
     event loop — every request, not only sales. At the store's 5000 ms timeout it would be five
     seconds. SQLite's own words: FULL and stronger modes "block concurrent writers while [running]"
     (<https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_wal_checkpoint>, fetched 2026-09-23);
   - on the writer's own connection inside its open transaction it is refused at once, errcode 6,
     `database table is locked`;
   - on the read-only connection it is refused, errcode 778 (`disk I/O error`);
   - on the writer's connection with NO transaction open, and the busy timeout set to 0 for that one
     statement, it took 0.1–0.9 ms, truncated the file to 0 bytes, and — with another connection
     holding a read — answered `busy: 1` in 0.2–0.6 ms instead of waiting.

   So the plan runs it **on the write connection, in a write-queue slot that opens no transaction,
   with a zero busy wait** (`checkpointTruncate`, Task 6). What the spec's sentence protects still
   holds: no sale waits on the bucket or on Litestream. A sale can wait behind the fold-back itself.
   With no Litestream attached that took milliseconds on the prototype ("With the daemon gone the
   same call took milliseconds and truncated the log to nothing", results note, S4), and 21.7 ms for
   a 310,145,392-byte side file in the run the rig's README records without the binary
   (`reclaim-control="ms=21.7 … wal=310145392->0"`, `bench/sqlite-failover/README.md`).
2. **§4.5's fallback "the generation name gains a per-node counter" is not needed.** Since §4.4 the
   name carries its opening time and opening starts with a create-only marker, so a new generation
   after each pause already has a distinct name, and a repeat is refused rather than overwritten. The
   plan opens a new generation per pause with no counter (only if Task 4's `RESTART_RESYNCS` is false).
3. **§7 names `scripts/alert-codes.test.ts` for the area claims; that guard covers RECORDED INCIDENT
   codes** (`INCIDENT_CODE_SOURCES`, lines 24-36). The four stream codes are ONGOING alerts built by a
   source, whose area is the source's own `area: "backup"` (`apps/server/src/alert-sources.ts:60`),
   and whose wording guard is `scripts/ongoing-alert-codes.test.ts` (it scans
   `apps/server/src/alert-sources.ts` for `code: "…"` literals). No module `alerts.events` claim is
   needed or possible for them.
4. **Unstated in §4.4 and needed:** what "its first full copy has landed" means in bucket terms, and
   how a new generation is made to start with one. Settled here from Litestream 0.5.17's source
   (release tarball of the tag, read 2026-09-23) and the rig's recorded keys: Litestream writes
   `<replica path>/<level as 4 hex digits>/<minTXID>-<maxTXID>.ltx` (`s3/replica_client.go:688`;
   `bench/sqlite-failover/src/copy-up.ts:47` records `venues/v1/gen-1-box-a/0000/0000000000000001-0000000000000001.ltx`);
   an LTX file whose first transaction is 1 is a snapshot (`IsSnapshot` is `MinTXID == 1`,
   `github.com/superfly/ltx@v0.5.2/ltx.go:198`); and a restore with no level-9 snapshot follows the
   contiguous chain from transaction 1 (`CalcRestorePlan`, `replica.go:1514`). And Litestream keeps its
   own position in a directory beside the database, `.venue.db-litestream` (`db.go:312`,
   `litestream.go:20`); with that directory still describing an OLD generation, an empty new replica
   path is filled from the local position onwards. Its own reset "removes local LTX files, forcing a
   fresh snapshot on next sync" (`ResetLocalState`, `db.go:522`). The plan deletes that directory
   before starting Litestream into a new generation. That is read from source, not run; Task 10's loop
   test is the first real run of it.
5. **Unstated consequence:** Litestream 0.5.17 creates two tables inside the database it streams,
   `_litestream_seq` and `_litestream_lock` (`db.go:1085-1092`), and writes to the first one. So
   `venue.db` on a streaming box, every archive taken from it, and every copy restored from the bucket
   carry two tables no migration made. Nothing in Tasks 6-7 reads `sqlite_master` wholesale; Tasks 9
   and 10 should check whatever of theirs does.
6. **Not measured, and the side-file limit does not cover it:** whether Litestream's local directory
   (`.venue.db-litestream`) also grows while the bucket is unreachable. The limit in §4.5 is on the
   `-wal` file, which is what S4 measured. Task 4 could read that directory's size in measurement 1.
7. **§7 "listing the live generation's newest file" has to choose a level.** Listing the whole
   generation each minute would page through every compacted file kept for 7 days — at the default
   30-second level-1 interval that is of the order of 20,000 objects (arithmetic, not a measurement).
   The plan lists `0000/` (level 0) each minute and `0001/` only when a commit has waited longer than
   level 0 keeps a file. Litestream's docs: `l0-retention` is the "Minimum time to retain L0 files
   after they have been compacted into L1 … Defaults to 5m" (<https://litestream.io/reference/config/>,
   fetched 2026-09-23); the plan's config sets it explicitly so the figure is ours, not a default.

#### Open questions

1. **The side-file limit is set against a measurement, not against the box's disk.** §4.5 asks for a
   limit "set in the plan against the box's disk, measured, not padded", and no box disk or partition
   size is recorded anywhere in the repository (the results note says so under S4; the till note
   `2026-09-18-handheld-and-till-hardware-decisions.md` quotes "128–256 GB SSD" for mini PCs as an
   estimate). The plan uses **256 MiB**, below the largest side file anything here has traded
   against: S4 grew it to 310,145,392 bytes and sales stayed at p95 0.297–0.333 ms with no drift. At
   S4's rig-model rate of 41,353 bytes a sale that is about 6,500 sales before Litestream is paused.
   Accept, or give a measured disk figure to set it against?
2. **Added safety rule: a box never replaces a pointer that names a HIGHER term than its own**; it
   refuses and raises `backup.stream_refused` instead. Without it, an old box that comes back after a
   rebuild reads the rebuilt box's pointer at startup and, if the rebuilt box does not write in
   between, moves the pointer back to itself with a perfectly valid conditional write. Keep?

---


### Notes from draft-task8-9.md

# Slice 2 plan — draft for Tasks 8 and 9

Drafted 2026-09-23 against `main` at `cb809f1b5`. Every path, function and line range named below
was read on that commit unless it is marked **new** or is a name another task produces (listed under
each task's "Consumes").

**Split.** Task 8 is two pull requests (8a server, 8b dashboard) and Task 9 is three (9a first start
after a rebuild, 9b the restore path and command line, 9c the setup wizard). Each is a PR a reviewer
could reject on its own; the order is 8a → 8b, and 9a → 9b → 9c. 9a lands first on purpose: it
only ACTS on a marker file that 9b is the first thing to write, so it is inert until 9b lands, and 9b
never leaves a rebuilt box without the certificate re-issue.

---

#### Contract changes

1. **`RestoreRequest`'s archive variant has an OPTIONAL `kind`.** The contract makes it
   `{ kind: "archive"; … }`. `apps/server/src/restore-request.test.ts` stages
   `{ artifact, recoveryKey, environment }` with no `kind` (four cases) and asserts the marker JSON
   `toEqual({ version: 1, environment: "production" })`; `apps/server/src/setup-api.test.ts:1600`
   asserts `stageRestore` was called with exactly those three keys. Both must pass unchanged
   (CLAUDE.md: preserve behavioural assertions), so the union is
   `{ kind?: "archive"; artifact; recoveryKey; environment } | { kind: "stream"; databasePath; entries; environment }`
   and an archive marker stays byte-identical.
2. **`restoreFromStream` is split.** The contract names one function for spec §5.1 steps 2–5. The
   wizard must run those steps in the SETUP process (so a failure changes nothing) and the
   destructive write after the restart, in the entrypoint, like the archive path. So 9b produces
   `prepareStreamRestore` (steps 2–5, no write outside a scratch folder), `writeStreamRestore` (the
   gate, the guard and `writeValidated`), and `restoreFromStream` (both, for the command line).
3. **`validateEntries` is new in `apps/server/src/restore.ts`** — the post-decrypt half of
   `validateArtifact`, so the stream source runs "the same compatibility gate, the same entry-name
   guard" (spec §5.1 step 6) rather than a copy. `validateArtifact` becomes decrypt + unpack +
   `validateEntries`; its behaviour and its tests are unchanged.
4. **The venue id has no source in the contract.** `SupervisorDeps.venueId` is named but nothing in
   the tree is called a venue id (`grep -rn venueId apps/server/src packages/membership/src` finds
   nothing). This draft uses the node's location id — `config.till.locationId`, the
   `WAITRON_TILL_LOCATION_ID` in `trading.env` (`apps/server/src/trading-config.ts:48`) — in the kit.
   **Task 6 must use the same value** for `SupervisorDeps.venueId`, or the kit points a rebuild at a
   prefix nothing streams to.
5. **Task 6 must export two things Task 9 consumes**, both in `@waitron/stream`:
   - `replicaUrl(bucket: BucketConfig, venueId: string, generation: string): string` — the replica
     URL its configuration writer puts under `dbs[0].replica.url`. The restore MUST read the path the
     supervisor writes; a second hand-built URL is exactly how the two would drift.
   - `resolveLitestreamBin(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string` — the binary path `SupervisorDeps.litestreamBin`
     comes from. The command line (`restore-command.ts`) never runs `loadConfig`, the same reason it
     resolves `WAITRON_VENUE_DIR` itself, so it needs the resolver, not a `ServerConfig` field. The
     setup-mode wiring calls the same resolver on the merged environment. 9b's command-line tests
     assume it returns a default path, rather than throwing, when its variable is unset.
6. **Task 5 must export `signPointer(body: StreamPointer, privateKeyPkcs8: string): SignedPointer`**,
   the inverse of `verifyPointer`. Task 9b's tests write a real signed pointer into a fake store; the
   contract gives the supervisor a `sign(bytes)` callback but no way to build a `SignedPointer` from a
   body, and a test that hand-assembles the signed bytes would pin Task 5's byte layout from outside.
7. **A lone recovery-key writer.** Spec §3.1: "switching it on sets one if there is none". The
   contract gives Task 2 `loadRecoveryKey(env)` (a reader) but no writer, and the only writer today,
   `writeBackupEnv` (`apps/server/src/backup-env-writer.ts:80-83`), requires a destination directory.
   8a adds `writeRecoveryKey(stateDir, key)` to `backup-env-writer.ts`. **If Task 2 already added a
   writer for a key without a destination, 8a uses Task 2's and drops its own.**
8. **`StreamHost` is new (8a).** The contract's `StreamSupervisor` has `start/stop/status` and no
   reload, and its `bucket` is fixed at construction. Saving new bucket settings must stop the running
   supervisor and start one on the new bucket, so 8a wraps it: `StreamHost` reads the bucket from the
   vault, and boot hands it a `makeSupervisor(bucket)` factory built from **exactly the deps Task 6
   passes today, minus `bucket`**. `/health` (Task 7) then reads `streamHost.status()` instead of the
   supervisor's.
9. **Route shapes under `/api/backup/stream`** (contract: "GET status/settings, PUT settings, POST
   test, GET kit") gain a `DELETE /api/backup/stream` (switch off). A setting that can be switched on
   from a screen has to be switchable off from it.
10. **New error codes** (each checked against its siblings' prefix; none collides with a code in
    `apps/server/src/errors.ts` or the contract's):
    - `backup.stream_test_failed { reason }`, `backup.stream_not_configured {}`,
      `backup.stream_signer_missing {}` — thrown by the stream settings routes, beside the
      existing `backup.*` admin codes (`errors.ts:1524-1600`). Distinct from Task 7's ALERT code
      `backup.stream_bucket_unusable`, whose params Task 7 owns.
    - `restore.stream_pointer_missing {}`, `restore.stream_pointer_unverified { reason }`,
      `restore.stream_source_live { lastChangeAt }`, `restore.stream_integrity_failed {}`,
      `restore.stream_state_missing { nodeId }` — beside the `restore.*` family (`errors.ts:1655-1733`).
    - `stream.kit_invalid { reason }` and `stream.restore_failed { exitCode }` — in
      `@waitron/stream`'s registry, beside Task 5's `stream.precondition_failed`.
11. **Dashboard subscription:** `getStreamSettings` refreshes on the existing `backup_status`
    subscription name (`apps/dashboard/src/api/live-queries.ts:112`), so no new server source name.

#### Spec problems

None that block building. Two orderings differ from the spec's numbering, deliberately, and are
stated so a reviewer comparing plan to spec does not read them as drift:

- **The pointer's signature is verified BEFORE Litestream downloads the generation** (spec §5.1 lists
  the download as step 2 and the verification as step 3). A pointer is what names the generation, so
  checking it first means an unverified pointer never directs a download; nothing on the box changes
  in either order.
- **The "old box still looks alive" check (step 4) also runs before the download**, for the same
  reason: it is a listing, and it can refuse before the slow step.

#### Open questions

1. **Should an ARCHIVE restore also re-issue the server certificate and bump the membership term on
   first start?** The spec asks it only of the bucket rebuild (§5.1 step 7), but an archive restored
   onto new hardware carries the dead box's leaf in `secrets/tls/server.crt` too
   (`apps/server/src/state-secrets.ts:15-22`), so it presents a certificate naming the old IP in the
   same way. This draft writes the first-start marker for the STREAM source only, as specified.
   Extending it to the archive path is one line in `writeValidated`'s caller; it is the owner's call
   because it changes the existing archive path's behaviour.
2. **What happens to a venue that streams but does not archive when the owner later turns archives
   on?** The backup screen's "Turn on backups" mints a NEW recovery key by default
   (`apps/dashboard/src/screens/backup-screen.ts:254-275`), which rotates the key the recovery kit
   carries. 8b shows the "your recovery key changed — download the new kit" banner when that
   happens, so nothing is silently lost, but the owner may prefer the archive wizard to REUSE the
   streaming key instead of minting one. That is a change to the backup wizard, not to these tasks.

---

#### The device-address check (spec §5.1: "the plan checks each … and states any that would need a human")

Established by reading on 2026-09-23 (not run on hardware). The rebuilt box keeps the hostname
`waitron.local`, its certificate authority and its node id; its LAN IP address may change.

| Device | How it finds the box | Finds a changed address without a human? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Till, handheld, kitchen screen (all the same till SPA; `packages/layouts/src/canvas.ts:9` lists the `kds` and phone form factors) | The page's own origin: `new ServerRouter({ origin: location.origin, … })` (`apps/till/src/main.ts:46`), plus the membership document's `contactUrl` list saved in `localStorage` (`apps/till/src/server-router.ts`). The device cookie is host-only (`apps/server/src/device-session.ts`, `cookieDomainFor`) | **Opened at `https://waitron.local`: yes** — mDNS answers with the new address on every query (`apps/server/src/mdns.ts` calls `getAddresses()` per query; `boot.ts:753` passes `config.boxAddresses ?? listBoxIpv4()`), and the cookie is keyed to the name. On iPhones this rests on `.local` resolving, which the appliance design lists as unverified (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-appliance-onboarding-design.md`, §7: "iOS `.local` reliability is [open]"). **Opened at an IP address (the trust page's QR code): no** — the old address is dead and its cookie is not sent to a new address. A person must open the device again at the new address and set it up as a device again. |
| Print agent on the box itself (the default) | `WAITRON_SERVER_URL`, defaulting to `https://127.0.0.1` (`deploy/compose.yml:117`, read at `apps/print-agent/src/config.ts:31`) | **Yes** — loopback does not depend on the LAN address, and `127.0.0.1` is always in the leaf (`apps/server/src/box-secrets.ts:141`). |
| Print agent on another computer | `WAITRON_PRINT_AGENT_SERVER_URL`, or the "Server address" saved on the agent's own page on port 9110 | **Only if it was given `waitron.local`, and even then not established**: the agent image installs nothing that resolves `.local` names (`deploy/Dockerfile:40-43` installs `bluez`). **Given an IP address: no** — a person changes the Server address on the agent's page (port 9110). |
| Dashboard in a browser | Its own origin (`apps/dashboard/src/main.ts:39`, `new DashboardApi("", …)`) | By name: yes. By IP: the manager types the new address. |

**What 9a's certificate re-issue changes in that table:** before it, the rebuilt box's leaf still
names the DEAD box's IP (the leaf is minted only when `tls/server.key` is absent,
`box-secrets.ts:133`, and the archive and the locked row both carry it), so even a person who found
the new IP would meet a certificate error. After 9a the leaf names this machine's addresses, which is
what makes the "open it again at the new address" instruction above workable.

9c puts the "needs a human" rows into the wizard's final screen text.

---


### Notes from draft-task10.md

# Slice 2 plan — Task 10 draft (loop test, S3 test server, documentation sweep)

#### Contract changes

Task 10 consumes these names. The contract does not fix them, so the plan assembler must reconcile
each one with the Task 1, 3, 6, 8 and 9 drafts. If a draft chose a different name, use that name
here too.

1. **`LITESTREAM_VERSION` is exported from `@waitron/stream`** (owned by Task 6). The contract only
   says "Litestream pin: `0.5.17`". The loop test compares `litestream version` output against this
   export, so the pin is written in one place only.
2. **`scripts/setup-litestream.mjs` installs to `<repo>/.bin/litestream`, and `apps/server` reads the
   binary's path from `WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN`** (Task 6). The contract names the script but not
   where it installs or how the server finds the binary. The loop test's resolver defaults to
   `<repo>/.bin/litestream` and passes `WAITRON_LITESTREAM_BIN` to every boot and to the restore
   command. **Heads-up for Task 6:** the root Vitest project measures `scripts/**/*.mjs` against
   98/98/98/95 (`vitest.config.ts`, `coverage.include`). A setup script under `scripts/` therefore
   needs a root suite that covers it, and its entry block needs a `/* v8 ignore start */ … stop`
   pair. This draft's `scripts/setup-s3-test-server.mjs` shows the shape.
3. **`restoreGeneration(deps: { litestreamBin: string; bucket: BucketConfig; venueId: string;
   generation: string; outPath: string }): Promise<void>` is exported from `@waitron/stream`** (Task 6
   or Task 9: whichever writes spec §5.1 step 2's "Litestream restores the latest point of the named
   generation into a side file"). It throws when Litestream exits non-zero. The loop test restores
   through the product's own call rather than writing a second Litestream config.
4. **The bucket command-line flags are `waitron-restore --from-bucket <kit-file>` and
   `--confirm-old-box-gone`** (Task 9). Spec §5.2 names the first. The second is this draft's
   proposal. Spec §5.1 step 4 requires the owner to confirm the old box is gone whenever the live
   generation changed in the last ten minutes, and in the loop test it always has. The test calls
   `runRestore({ argv, env, out })` from `apps/server/src/restore-command.ts`, which exists today.
   It expects exit code 0.
5. **A second `openVenueDatabase` of the same folder, made from the same process, still succeeds**
   (Task 3). Spec §6's lock refuses only another process. Existing suites already depend on a
   second open in the same process: `apps/server/src/till-reroute-e2e.test.ts` seeds through its
   own handle while `startServer` holds the folder. The loop test records sales the same way, with
   `recordOneSale` (`apps/server/scripts/record-one-sale.ts`) running alongside a booted server.
6. **Boot starts streaming when a `backup.stream` credential exists and a recovery key is set** (Tasks 6
   and 8). The loop test switches streaming on with `putCredential(tx, ring, { purpose: "backup.stream",
   value: { endpoint, region, bucket, prefix, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey } })`. If Task 8's "switch
   on" does more than store the credential (for example, if it mints the venue id), Step 5 calls
   Task 8's function in place of `putCredential`, and nothing else changes.
7. **`StartedServer.close()` stops Litestream with SIGTERM, and only after every writer has
   stopped** (Task 6). The check "a restore of B's generation equals B's database" runs after
   B is closed, so it needs that stop order. Measured 2026-09-23 in the scratchpad, Litestream 0.5.17
   darwin/arm64 against versitygw 1.8.0: a write made moments before SIGTERM was in a later restore
   in 2 of 2 runs, and the same write before SIGKILL was missing (1 of 1). The commands are under
   "Receipts" below.
8. **`probeBucket(store)` resolves to exactly `{ ok: true }` on a good bucket** (Task 5). This is
   the loop test's first assertion.
9. **New names this task introduces**, all used by tests only:
   - `WAITRON_VERSITYGW_BIN` overrides where the S3 server binary is found.
   - `WAITRON_REQUIRE_STREAM_BINARIES=1` makes a missing binary fail the test instead of skipping it.
   - `<repo>/.bin/` is gitignored and holds both downloaded binaries.

The venue id is **not** consumed from any task. The loop test reads it off the bucket, from the one
`venues/<id>/current.json` key there. That keeps the test independent of where Task 8 stores the id.

#### Spec problems

1. **Litestream 0.5.17 adds two tables to the database it streams, and a hidden directory beside the
   file.** Neither the spec nor the topology design says so. Measured 2026-09-23 with the pinned
   binary against versitygw 1.8.0: the streamed file gained `_litestream_seq` and
   `_litestream_lock`, and `.venue.db-litestream/ltx/0/…` appeared next to it. The restored copy
   carried both tables. What this changes:
   - Spec §8.2 says "restore from B's generation equals B's database". The loop test therefore
     compares every table except those two, which are Litestream's own bookkeeping.
   - `apps/server/src/db-wipe.ts` (`VENUE_FILES`) and the restore that places a database into the
     venue folder do not know about `.venue.db-litestream/`. What happens when a stale one survives
     next to a replaced `venue.db` has **not** been tested. Task 6 or Task 9 has to decide, and
     measure it.
   - Any claim that lists what the venue folder holds is now incomplete (the docs sweep, Step 12).
2. **"The prototype rig stays as the MinIO reference" (spec §8.2) refers to a frozen upstream.**
   MinIO's README now opens with *"THIS REPOSITORY IS NO LONGER MAINTAINED."* It also says *"The
   MinIO community edition is now distributed as source code only. We will no longer provide
   pre-compiled binary releases for the community version."* `https://dl.min.io/server/minio/release/linux-amd64/`
   answers HTTP 410. (Both fetched with `curl` on 2026-09-23.) The rig pulls a container image
   pinned by digest from quay.io, and I have not established whether that image stays pullable.
   Nothing in this task depends on MinIO.
3. **The equality check also asserts that a clean shutdown uploads the last writes.** Spec §4.1
   says only that the supervisor "stops it at shutdown". See contract change 7. If Task 6 chose
   another stop order, the loop test fails when B is compared after its close. The fix then belongs
   in the supervisor's stop order, not in the test.

#### Open questions

None. The choices below — versitygw, downloading the binaries on each run instead of caching them,
and running the test in every `apps/server` shard — are settled here with their reasons.

#### Receipts for the choices in this task

**The S3-compatible server is versitygw 1.8.0.** It was chosen by running each candidate, not only
by reading about it. A research seat checked every web source with `curl` (never WebFetch), and I
repeated the load-bearing runs myself. Everything ran on 127.0.0.1 on darwin/arm64 on 2026-09-23.
Every process was killed and its PID confirmed dead.

| Candidate | `If-None-Match: *` on an existing key | Stale `If-Match` | 20 parallel create-only writes | Pinned binary + checksum, linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64 | Download (linux/amd64) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **versitygw 1.8.0** | **412 (ran)** | **412 (ran)** | **1 × 200, 19 × 412 (ran)** | yes, SHA-256 in `checksums.txt` | 27,542,985 bytes |
| SeaweedFS 4.47 (`weed mini`) | 412 (ran) | 412 (ran) | 1 × 200, 19 × 412 (ran) | yes, but **MD5 only** | ~45.8 MB |
| MinIO RELEASE.2025-09-07 | 412 (ran) | 412 (ran) | 1 × 200, 19 × 412 (ran) | GitHub only. The repository is archived and dl.min.io answers 410. | 110,989,496 bytes |
| Garage 2.4.1 | **not supported** (read: issue #1052 is open, and a maintainer wrote *"adding this to Garage is not possible with our weak-consistency replication model"*) | — | — | linux only, no checksum | 71 MB |
| rclone 1.75.1 `serve s3` | **200, and the object was overwritten (ran)** | **200, overwritten (ran)** | 18 × 200, 2 × 500 | yes | ~31.5 MB |

Why versitygw:

- It behaves as AWS documents, including a 404 for `If-Match` on a missing key, where SeaweedFS
  returns 412. The AWS page (`https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html`,
  via `curl`) says: *"If there's an existing object, the write operation fails, resulting in a 412
  Precondition Failed response."*
- It is one process on one port and starts in about 0.2 s. `weed mini` listened on eleven ports,
  one of them on every interface.
- Its release publishes SHA-256 checksums. `checksums.txt` for v1.8.0 lists
  `2ba2c734…3467  versitygw_v1.8.0_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz`, and I re-downloaded that tarball and got
  the same SHA-256. The darwin/arm64 checksum also matched.
- Its licence is Apache-2.0, and v1.8.0 was released on 2026-09-04.

Litestream 0.5.17 runs against versitygw. I measured this myself on 2026-09-23 with the pinned
darwin/arm64 binary (its SHA-256 matched the GitHub API's `digest` for the asset):

- `replicate -once` twice (a write between the two runs), then `restore`: exit 0 each time, and all
  four rows were restored. The failing case would have been a non-zero exit or three rows.
- A `replicate` daemon, a write three seconds later, then `restore` while the daemon ran: both rows
  were present, and the daemon logged no `ERROR` or `WARN`.

The same checks also passed with `versitygw … posix --sidecar <dir>`, where object metadata goes to
a plain directory instead of extended attributes. That covered the conditional writes (412 / 200 /
412, body `v3`) and the daemon plus restore (both rows). **The helper therefore always starts it with
`--sidecar`.** The loop test does not rely on the CI runner's temporary filesystem supporting
extended attributes, which I could not check from darwin. A pre-created directory under the gateway
root works as a bucket (PUT 200, then 412 on a conditional rewrite). Bucket names shorter than three
characters are refused with `InvalidBucketName`.

**If versitygw's conditional writes turn out wrong on Linux**, the loop test's first assertion
(`probeBucket`) fails and prints the probe's reason. Nothing gets past it. The recorded fallback is
SeaweedFS 4.47, which passed the same run. Its costs are MD5-only checksums, eleven ports and a
three-second stop, and the next session weighs those before swapping.

**CI downloads both binaries on every run instead of caching them.** The repository's Actions cache
held 10,930,275,583 bytes across 907 entries (`gh api repos/:owner/:repo/actions/cache/usage`,
2026-09-23). Grouping the entries by key gives:

- Docker layers (`buildkit-*`): about 9,642 MB.
- The pnpm store (`node-cache-Linux-…`, 7 entries): about 766 MB.
- The Playwright browser (`playwright-Linux-1.63.0`): about 284 MB.

GitHub evicts the least recently used entry, so a new ~41 MB entry would compete with the pnpm store
and Playwright entries that every test job restores. Downloading instead costs each `test-server`
shard 13,540,484 bytes of Litestream (the release API's `size` field) plus 27,542,985 bytes of
versitygw, three shards per run. The time this adds has not been measured. A GitHub release outage
fails those shards, and the failure message names the URL.

**Where the test lives: `apps/server`.** The test needs the whole boot. The stream restore runs at
the next start, the rebuilt box re-issues its certificate and signs a membership document one term
higher (Task 9), and boot starts the supervisor (Task 6). It cannot live in `packages/stream`,
because `apps/server` depends on `@waitron/stream`. Importing the server from the stream package's
tests would close a workspace dependency loop, which `scripts/workspace-cycles.test.ts` refuses
(CLAUDE.md §3). `apps/server` is sharded three ways by test file, and I found no way to fix which
shard receives a file. So every `test-server` shard installs both binaries.
